\section{Sawtooth sums and the main term for one modulus}\label{sec:sawtooth}

\subsection{Sawtooth sums}

The function $B(u)=\fr u(1-\fr u)$ is continuous, $1$-periodic, takes values in $[0,\frac14]$, and satisfies $B(u)=u-u^2$ for $0\le u\le1$. The sums we need are $\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)$ and weighted versions of them. Their size $\asymp\sqrt Z$ has two sources: the terms with $s>\sqrt Z$, where $B(Z/s^2)=Z/s^2-Z^2/s^4$, and the terms with $s\le\sqrt Z$, where $B$ oscillates. The natural approximation is the integral $\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z$ (substitute $u=\sqrt Z\,w$). For $q\in\N$ put
\[
\kappa_q(t)=\kappa(t)\one[(t,q)=1],\qquad \Delta_q=\prod_p\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\one[p\nmid q]\frac{p}{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
For $p\nmid q$ the factor of $\Delta_q$ is $(p-1)^2(p+2)/(p(p^2-2))=1+O(p^{-2})$; there are finitely many other factors, so the product converges absolutely.

\begin{proposition}[Sawtooth sums]\label{prop:sawtooth}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $I=\int_0^\infty B(u^{-2})\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
\item For every real $Z>0$, $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$ with $c_1=60$.
\item For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_5(\eps)$ such that for all $q\in\N$ and real $Z>0$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-\Delta_q\,I\sqrt Z\Bigr|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^\eps Z^{1/3}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) The substitution $v=u^{-2}$ gives the second expression. The integral converges, because $B(v)\le v$ near $0$ and $B(v)\le\frac14$. Since $B$ is continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with $B'(v)=1-2\fr v$, integration by parts on $[0,X]$ gives
\[
\int_0^XB(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=\bigl[-2B(v)v^{-1/2}\bigr]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv .
\]
The boundary term tends to $0$, because $B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ near $0$ and $B(X)X^{-1/2}\le\frac14X^{-1/2}$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=2\lim_{N\to\infty}\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv$ along integers $N$. On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$ and $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$ of $v^{-1/2}$,
\[
\int_n^{n+1}B'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}\,dv,
\]
and summing over $0\le n<N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Bprime}
\int_0^NB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^Nm^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.
\end{equation}
Now apply \cref{lem:EM} on $(N,\infty)$ to $G(u)=u^{-s}$ with $\Re s>1$, using $\psi(N)=-\frac12$ and $\psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$:
\[
\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac s{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}\,du .
\]
The right-hand side is analytic in $\Re s>-1$, $s\ne1$, because the integral converges locally uniformly there. By uniqueness of analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$ plus the right-hand side in that region. At $s=-\frac12$ we have $s(s+1)=-\frac14$ and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}\,du|\le\frac16N^{-1/2}$, so
\[
\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bprime} shows that $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv\to-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. By the functional equation~\cite[Corollary~10.4]{MV2007} at $s=-\frac12$, $\zeta(-\frac12)=2^{-1/2}\pi^{-3/2}\Gamma(\frac32)\sin(-\frac\pi4)\zeta(\frac32)=-\zeta(\frac32)/(4\pi)$. So $I=\zeta(3/2)/\pi>0$, the value stated in~\eqref{eq:I}.

(b) \emph{The case $Z<1$.} Here $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z^{1/3}$. Also $0<I\sqrt Z<Z^{1/3}$, since $I<1$. The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.

\emph{The case $Z\ge1$.} Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$ and $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b1}
\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad \frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda .
\end{equation}
\emph{Small $s$.} Both $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)$ and $\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)\,du$ lie in $[0,T/4]\subset[0,\Lambda/4]$, so their difference is at most $\Lambda/4$. It therefore suffices to show
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b2}
\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du\Bigr|\le57\Lambda ,
\end{equation}
which gives the claim with $57+\frac14<60$.

\emph{A decomposition of $B$.} For real $w\ge0$ with $j=\lfloor w\rfloor$ we have $B(w)=(w-j)(1-w+j)=w-w^2+2jw-j-j^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^j2(w-k)=2jw-j^2-j$. Hence
\[
B(w)=w-w^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(w-k)_+,\qquad(v)_+=\max(v,0).
\]
Put $\Phi(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$, so that $B(Z/u^2)=\Phi(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only the $k<K_0$ contribute, and there are fewer than $K_0<4\Lambda$ of them. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ on $[T,R_k]$ with $R_k=\sqrt{Z/k}>T$, and $G_k=0$ on $[R_k,\infty)$.

\emph{Euler--Maclaurin.} Apply \cref{lem:EM} to $\Phi$ on $(T,\infty)$, and to $Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$ for each $k<K_0$. Use $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$ and $G_k(R_k)=0$, and add. Since $\int_T^\infty\Phi+2\sum_k\int_T^{R_k}G_k=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du$ (all integrals converge absolutely), this gives
\[
\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du+R_1+R_2+R_3+R_4+R_5,
\]
where, writing $G_k'$ and $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $R_1=\psi(T)\bigl[\Phi(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$. The individual terms here have size about $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $B(Z/T^2)\le\frac14$. So $|R_1|\le\frac18$. This is the one place where cancellation is essential.
\item $R_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[\Phi'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$, with $\Phi'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$ and $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By~\eqref{eq:b1}, $|\Phi'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$ and $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<128\Lambda$. So $|R_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
\item $R_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2\Phi''\,du$ with $\Phi''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$. So $|R_3|\le\frac1{12}(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
\item $R_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''\,du$ with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Zu^{-4}\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|R_4|\le\frac2{12}K_0\cdot16<\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
\item $R_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$ with $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<4\Lambda$, $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$ we get $|R_5|\le\frac2{12}\cdot2\cdot32\Lambda=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. These are the kinks of the $G_k$ at the points $R_k$. Summing over the $K_0\asymp Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is what produces the exponent $\frac13$.
\end{itemize}
Using $\Lambda\ge1$, the total is at most $(\frac18+\frac{272}{12}+12+\frac{32}3+\frac{32}3)\Lambda=\frac{449}8\Lambda<57\Lambda$, which proves~\eqref{eq:b2}.

(c) Fix $q$. The function $\kappa_q$ is multiplicative with $\kappa_q(p)=p^2/(p^2-2)$ for $p\nmid q$, $\kappa_q(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$ and $\kappa_q(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\beta=\mu*\kappa_q$, so that $\kappa_q=1*\beta$. Then $\beta$ is multiplicative, with $\beta(p^j)=\kappa_q(p^j)-\kappa_q(p^{j-1})$:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $p\mid q$: $\beta(p)=-1$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$;
\item for $p\nmid q$: $\beta(p)=\frac2{p^2-2}$, $\beta(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge3$.
\end{itemize}
\emph{Absolute convergence.} For $p\nmid q$, $\sum_j|\beta(p^j)|p^{-2j/3}\le\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}$, because $p^2/(p^2-2)\le2$. Hence
\[
\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\beta(n)|}{n^{2/3}}\le\prod_{p\mid q}\bigl(1+p^{-2/3}\bigr)\prod_p\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}\Bigr)\le C_\beta\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C_\beta C(\eps)q^\eps,
\]
with an absolute constant $C_\beta$, by \cref{lem:divisor}. Similarly $\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$ for each fixed $q$.

\emph{Rearrangement.} For $W>0$, $\sum_mB(W/m^2)\le\sum_m\min(\frac14,W/m^2)\le3\sqrt W$. Indeed, for $W<1$ the sum is at most $\zeta(2)W\le2\sqrt W$, and for $W\ge1$ it is at most $\frac14\sqrt W+W\cdot2/\sqrt W$ by \cref{lem:tail}. Hence $\sum_{n,m}|\beta(n)|B(Z/(nm)^2)\le3\sqrt Z\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$, and we may rearrange:
\[
\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)=\sum_{n,m\ge1}\beta(n)B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge1}\beta(n)\sum_{m\ge1}B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Main term.} Part (b) holds for every positive argument. Applying it with $Z/n^2$ in place of $Z$, and using $I\sqrt{Z/n^2}=I\sqrt Z/n$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_t\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-I\sqrt Z\sum_n\frac{\beta(n)}n\Bigr|\le c_1\sum_n|\beta(n)|\Bigl(\frac Z{n^2}\Bigr)^{1/3}=c_1\Sigma_{2/3}Z^{1/3}.
\]
\emph{The constant.} By~\eqref{eq:euler}, $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\prod_p\bigl(1+\beta(p)/p+\beta(p^2)/p^2\bigr)$. For $p\mid q$ the factor is $1-1/p$. For $p\nmid q$ it is
\[
1+\frac2{p(p^2-2)}-\frac1{p^2-2}=\frac{p^3-3p+2}{p(p^2-2)}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p(p^2-2)}=\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\frac p{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Hence $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\Delta_q$, and (c) holds with $c_5(\eps)=c_1C_\beta C(\eps)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The main term for one modulus}

\begin{proposition}[Asymptotics of $\MT$]\label{prop:MT}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_6(\eps)$ such that for all real $x>0$ and all $q\in\N$,
\[
\bigl|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\bigr|\le c_6(\eps)\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps},
\]
with $h$ as in~\eqref{eq:h}. In particular this holds for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Factorising $t$.} Fix $q$. Every squarefree $t$ factors uniquely as $t=t_0t_1t_2$, where $t_0$ is composed of primes $p\nmid q$, $t_1$ of primes $p\,\|\,q$, and $t_2$ of primes $p$ with $p^2\mid q$. Conversely, every such triple of squarefree numbers gives a squarefree $t$. Let $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ be the finite sets of admissible $t_1$ and $t_2$ (all of them divide $q$). For squarefree $t$, $\gcd(t^2,q)=\prod_{p\mid t}p^{\min(2,v_p(q))}=t_1t_2^2$, so
\[
m_t(q)=t_0^2t_1,\qquad\frac x{q\,m_t(q)}=\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\quad\text{with}\quad Z_1=\frac{x}{q\,t_1},\qquad \eta(t)m_t(q)=\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\kappa(t_0).
\]
By the absolute convergence in \cref{lem:eta} we may regroup:
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\,q\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\Sigma(t_1),\qquad\Sigma(t_1)=\sum_{t_0\ge1}\kappa_q(t_0)B\Bigl(\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Applying \cref{prop:sawtooth}(c).} With $Z=Z_1>0$ we get $\Sigma(t_1)=\Delta_qI\sqrt{Z_1}+\theta\,c_5(\eps)q^\eps Z_1^{1/3}$. Since $t_1\sqrt{Z_1}=\sqrt{x/q}\,t_1^{1/2}$ and $t_1Z_1^{1/3}=(x/q)^{1/3}t_1^{2/3}$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\Delta_qI\sqrt{xq}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)+R,
\]
\[
|R|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^{1+\eps}\Bigl(\frac xq\Bigr)^{1/3}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2),
\]
where we used $A_0\le1$. By~\eqref{eq:eta-bound}, $\sum_{t_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-4/3})$ and $\sum_{t_2}\eta(t_2)\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-2})$, both absolute constants. So $|R|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$.

\emph{The constant is $h(q)$.} The two finite sums are Euler products over the primes dividing $q$:
\[
\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}=\prod_{p\|q}\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr),\qquad\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)=\prod_{p^2\mid q}\Bigl(1+\frac1{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Multiplying the absolutely convergent products $A_0$ and $\Delta_q$ factor by factor, the local factor at $p$ of the main coefficient is
\begin{align*}
p\nmid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac p{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2+p-2)}{p^3}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3}=a_p,\\
p\,\|\,q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3}=b_p,\\
p^2\mid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac1{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-1)}{p^3}=c_p .
\end{align*}
Together with the factor $I$, this is exactly $h(q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Since $b_p/a_p\ge1-1/p$ and $c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2)\ge1-1/p$, we have $h(q)\ge IA_h\,\varphi(q)/q\gg_\eps q^{-\eps}$, where $A_h=\prod_pa_p>0$ (\cref{prop:poly}(0)). So \cref{prop:MT} gives, for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=h(q)\sqrt{xq}\,\bigl(1+O_\eps(x^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6})\bigr),
\]
because the relative error is $\ll_\eps q^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6}$ and $q^{2\eps}\le x^{2\eps}$ for $q\le x$. (Without the restriction $q\le x$ the display can fail. Since $0\le q\,m\,B(x/(qm))\le x$ and $\sum_t\eta(t)<\infty$ (\cref{lem:eta}), \eqref{eq:MT} gives $0\le\MT(x;q)\ll x$ for all $x>0$. This is why the asymptotic formula of \cref{thm:main}(iii) requires $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, whereas the error term in~(ii), which keeps $\MT$ unexpanded, has no such restriction. The numerical data in \cref{sec:numerics} suggest that, after summation over the moduli, the secondary term has relative size roughly proportional to $\sqrt{Y/x}$. That is consistent with, but sharper than, the proved bound.
\end{remark}

\section{Sawtooth sums and the main term for one modulus}\label{sec:sawtooth}

\subsection{Sawtooth sums}

The function $B(u)=\fr u(1-\fr u)$ is continuous, $1$-periodic, takes values in $[0,\frac14]$, and satisfies $B(u)=u-u^2$ for $0\le u\le1$. The sums we need are $\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)$ and weighted versions of them. Their size $\asymp\sqrt Z$ has two sources: the terms with $s>\sqrt Z$, where $B(Z/s^2)=Z/s^2-Z^2/s^4$, and the terms with $s\le\sqrt Z$, where $B$ oscillates. The natural approximation is the integral $\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z$ (substitute $u=\sqrt Z\,w$). For $q\in\N$ put
\[
\kappa_q(t)=\kappa(t)\one[(t,q)=1],\qquad \Delta_q=\prod_p\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\one[p\nmid q]\frac{p}{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
For $p\nmid q$ the factor of $\Delta_q$ is $(p-1)^2(p+2)/(p(p^2-2))=1+O(p^{-2})$; there are finitely many other factors, so the product converges absolutely.

\begin{proposition}[Sawtooth sums]\label{prop:sawtooth}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $I=\int_0^\infty B(u^{-2})\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
\item For every real $Z>0$, $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$ with $c_1=60$.
\item For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_5(\eps)$ such that for all $q\in\N$ and real $Z>0$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-\Delta_q\,I\sqrt Z\Bigr|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^\eps Z^{1/3}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) The substitution $v=u^{-2}$ gives the second expression. The integral converges, because $B(v)\le v$ near $0$ and $B(v)\le\frac14$. Since $B$ is continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with $B'(v)=1-2\fr v$, integration by parts on $[0,X]$ gives
\[
\int_0^XB(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=\bigl[-2B(v)v^{-1/2}\bigr]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv .
\]
The boundary term tends to $0$, because $B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ near $0$ and $B(X)X^{-1/2}\le\frac14X^{-1/2}$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=2\lim_{N\to\infty}\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv$ along integers $N$. On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$ and $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$ of $v^{-1/2}$,
\[
\int_n^{n+1}B'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}\,dv,
\]
and summing over $0\le n<N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Bprime}
\int_0^NB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^Nm^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.
\end{equation}
Now apply \cref{lem:EM} on $(N,\infty)$ to $G(u)=u^{-s}$ with $\Re s>1$, using $\psi(N)=-\frac12$ and $\psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$:
\[
\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac s{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}\,du .
\]
The right-hand side is analytic in $\Re s>-1$, $s\ne1$, because the integral converges locally uniformly there. By uniqueness of analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$ plus the right-hand side in that region. At $s=-\frac12$ we have $s(s+1)=-\frac14$ and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}\,du|\le\frac16N^{-1/2}$, so
\[
\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bprime} shows that $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv\to-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. By the functional equation~\cite[Corollary~10.4]{MV2007} at $s=-\frac12$, $\zeta(-\frac12)=2^{-1/2}\pi^{-3/2}\Gamma(\frac32)\sin(-\frac\pi4)\zeta(\frac32)=-\zeta(\frac32)/(4\pi)$. So $I=\zeta(3/2)/\pi>0$, the value stated in~\eqref{eq:I}.

(b) \emph{The case $Z<1$.} Here $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z^{1/3}$. Also $0<I\sqrt Z<Z^{1/3}$, since $I<1$. The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.

\emph{The case $Z\ge1$.} Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$ and $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b1}
\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad \frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda .
\end{equation}
\emph{Small $s$.} Both $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)$ and $\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)\,du$ lie in $[0,T/4]\subset[0,\Lambda/4]$, so their difference is at most $\Lambda/4$. It therefore suffices to show
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b2}
\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du\Bigr|\le57\Lambda ,
\end{equation}
which gives the claim with $57+\frac14<60$.

\emph{A decomposition of $B$.} For real $w\ge0$ with $j=\lfloor w\rfloor$ we have $B(w)=(w-j)(1-w+j)=w-w^2+2jw-j-j^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^j2(w-k)=2jw-j^2-j$. Hence
\[
B(w)=w-w^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(w-k)_+,\qquad(v)_+=\max(v,0).
\]
Put $\Phi(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$, so that $B(Z/u^2)=\Phi(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only the $k<K_0$ contribute, and there are fewer than $K_0<4\Lambda$ of them. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ on $[T,R_k]$ with $R_k=\sqrt{Z/k}>T$, and $G_k=0$ on $[R_k,\infty)$.

\emph{Euler--Maclaurin.} Apply \cref{lem:EM} to $\Phi$ on $(T,\infty)$, and to $Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$ for each $k<K_0$. Use $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$ and $G_k(R_k)=0$, and add. Since $\int_T^\infty\Phi+2\sum_k\int_T^{R_k}G_k=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du$ (all integrals converge absolutely), this gives
\[
\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du+R_1+R_2+R_3+R_4+R_5,
\]
where, writing $G_k'$ and $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $R_1=\psi(T)\bigl[\Phi(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$. The individual terms here have size about $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $B(Z/T^2)\le\frac14$. So $|R_1|\le\frac18$. This is the one place where cancellation is essential.
\item $R_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[\Phi'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$, with $\Phi'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$ and $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By~\eqref{eq:b1}, $|\Phi'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$ and $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<128\Lambda$. So $|R_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
\item $R_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2\Phi''\,du$ with $\Phi''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$. So $|R_3|\le\frac1{12}(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
\item $R_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''\,du$ with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Zu^{-4}\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|R_4|\le\frac2{12}K_0\cdot16<\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
\item $R_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$ with $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<4\Lambda$, $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$ we get $|R_5|\le\frac2{12}\cdot2\cdot32\Lambda=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. These are the kinks of the $G_k$ at the points $R_k$. Summing over the $K_0\asymp Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is what produces the exponent $\frac13$.
\end{itemize}
Using $\Lambda\ge1$, the total is at most $(\frac18+\frac{272}{12}+12+\frac{32}3+\frac{32}3)\Lambda=\frac{449}8\Lambda<57\Lambda$, which proves~\eqref{eq:b2}.

(c) Fix $q$. The function $\kappa_q$ is multiplicative with $\kappa_q(p)=p^2/(p^2-2)$ for $p\nmid q$, $\kappa_q(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$ and $\kappa_q(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\beta=\mu*\kappa_q$, so that $\kappa_q=1*\beta$. Then $\beta$ is multiplicative, with $\beta(p^j)=\kappa_q(p^j)-\kappa_q(p^{j-1})$:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $p\mid q$: $\beta(p)=-1$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$;
\item for $p\nmid q$: $\beta(p)=\frac2{p^2-2}$, $\beta(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge3$.
\end{itemize}
\emph{Absolute convergence.} For $p\nmid q$, $\sum_j|\beta(p^j)|p^{-2j/3}\le\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}$, because $p^2/(p^2-2)\le2$. Hence
\[
\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\beta(n)|}{n^{2/3}}\le\prod_{p\mid q}\bigl(1+p^{-2/3}\bigr)\prod_p\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}\Bigr)\le C_\beta\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C_\beta C(\eps)q^\eps,
\]
with an absolute constant $C_\beta$, by \cref{lem:divisor}. Similarly $\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$ for each fixed $q$.

\emph{Rearrangement.} For $W>0$, $\sum_mB(W/m^2)\le\sum_m\min(\frac14,W/m^2)\le3\sqrt W$. Indeed, for $W<1$ the sum is at most $\zeta(2)W\le2\sqrt W$, and for $W\ge1$ it is at most $\frac14\sqrt W+W\cdot2/\sqrt W$ by \cref{lem:tail}. Hence $\sum_{n,m}|\beta(n)|B(Z/(nm)^2)\le3\sqrt Z\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$, and we may rearrange:
\[
\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)=\sum_{n,m\ge1}\beta(n)B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge1}\beta(n)\sum_{m\ge1}B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Main term.} Part (b) holds for every positive argument. Applying it with $Z/n^2$ in place of $Z$, and using $I\sqrt{Z/n^2}=I\sqrt Z/n$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_t\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-I\sqrt Z\sum_n\frac{\beta(n)}n\Bigr|\le c_1\sum_n|\beta(n)|\Bigl(\frac Z{n^2}\Bigr)^{1/3}=c_1\Sigma_{2/3}Z^{1/3}.
\]
\emph{The constant.} By~\eqref{eq:euler}, $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\prod_p\bigl(1+\beta(p)/p+\beta(p^2)/p^2\bigr)$. For $p\mid q$ the factor is $1-1/p$. For $p\nmid q$ it is
\[
1+\frac2{p(p^2-2)}-\frac1{p^2-2}=\frac{p^3-3p+2}{p(p^2-2)}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p(p^2-2)}=\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\frac p{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Hence $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\Delta_q$, and (c) holds with $c_5(\eps)=c_1C_\beta C(\eps)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The main term for one modulus}

\begin{proposition}[Asymptotics of $\MT$]\label{prop:MT}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_6(\eps)$ such that for all real $x>0$ and all $q\in\N$,
\[
\bigl|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\bigr|\le c_6(\eps)\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps},
\]
with $h$ as in~\eqref{eq:h}. In particular this holds for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Factorising $t$.} Fix $q$. Every squarefree $t$ factors uniquely as $t=t_0t_1t_2$, where $t_0$ is composed of primes $p\nmid q$, $t_1$ of primes $p\,\|\,q$, and $t_2$ of primes $p$ with $p^2\mid q$. Conversely, every such triple of squarefree numbers gives a squarefree $t$. Let $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ be the finite sets of admissible $t_1$ and $t_2$ (all of them divide $q$). For squarefree $t$, $\gcd(t^2,q)=\prod_{p\mid t}p^{\min(2,v_p(q))}=t_1t_2^2$, so
\[
m_t(q)=t_0^2t_1,\qquad\frac x{q\,m_t(q)}=\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\quad\text{with}\quad Z_1=\frac{x}{q\,t_1},\qquad \eta(t)m_t(q)=\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\kappa(t_0).
\]
By the absolute convergence in \cref{lem:eta} we may regroup:
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\,q\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\Sigma(t_1),\qquad\Sigma(t_1)=\sum_{t_0\ge1}\kappa_q(t_0)B\Bigl(\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Applying \cref{prop:sawtooth}(c).} With $Z=Z_1>0$ we get $\Sigma(t_1)=\Delta_qI\sqrt{Z_1}+\theta\,c_5(\eps)q^\eps Z_1^{1/3}$. Since $t_1\sqrt{Z_1}=\sqrt{x/q}\,t_1^{1/2}$ and $t_1Z_1^{1/3}=(x/q)^{1/3}t_1^{2/3}$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\Delta_qI\sqrt{xq}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)+R,
\]
\[
|R|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^{1+\eps}\Bigl(\frac xq\Bigr)^{1/3}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2),
\]
where we used $A_0\le1$. By~\eqref{eq:eta-bound}, $\sum_{t_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-4/3})$ and $\sum_{t_2}\eta(t_2)\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-2})$, both absolute constants. So $|R|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$.

\emph{The constant is $h(q)$.} The two finite sums are Euler products over the primes dividing $q$:
\[
\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}=\prod_{p\|q}\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr),\qquad\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)=\prod_{p^2\mid q}\Bigl(1+\frac1{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Multiplying the absolutely convergent products $A_0$ and $\Delta_q$ factor by factor, the local factor at $p$ of the main coefficient is
\begin{align*}
p\nmid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac p{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2+p-2)}{p^3}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3}=a_p,\\
p\,\|\,q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3}=b_p,\\
p^2\mid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac1{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-1)}{p^3}=c_p .
\end{align*}
Together with the factor $I$, this is exactly $h(q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Since $b_p/a_p\ge1-1/p$ and $c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2)\ge1-1/p$, we have $h(q)\ge IA_h\,\varphi(q)/q\gg_\eps q^{-\eps}$, where $A_h=\prod_pa_p>0$ (\cref{prop:poly}(0)). So \cref{prop:MT} gives, for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=h(q)\sqrt{xq}\,\bigl(1+O_\eps(x^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6})\bigr),
\]
because the relative error is $\ll_\eps q^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6}$ and $q^{2\eps}\le x^{2\eps}$ for $q\le x$. (Without the restriction $q\le x$ the display can fail. Since $0\le q\,m\,B(x/(qm))\le x$ and $\sum_t\eta(t)<\infty$ (\cref{lem:eta}), \eqref{eq:MT} gives $0\le\MT(x;q)\ll x$ for all $x>0$. Hence $\MT(x;1)/(h(1)\sqrt x)\to0$ as $x\to0$, whereas for $\eps>1/12$ the displayed error term $x^{2\eps}x^{-1/6}$ tends to $0$.) The relative error is not small when $q\asymp x$. This is why the asymptotic formula of \cref{thm:main}(iii) requires $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, whereas the error term in~(ii), which keeps $\MT$ unexpanded, has no such restriction. The numerical data in \cref{sec:numerics} suggest that, after summation over the moduli, the secondary term has relative size roughly proportional to $\sqrt{Y/x}$. That is consistent with, but sharper than, the proved bound.
\end{remark}

1	# Proof of P8 (averages over polynomial moduli)
     2	
     3	No dependencies and no papers are needed beyond standard facts: the functional equation of $\zeta$ (Riemann; e.g. Montgomery–Vaughan, *Multiplicative Number Theory I*, 2007, Ch. 10), the divisor bound $\tau(n)\ll_\varepsilon n^{\varepsilon}$, and the Chinese remainder theorem. Nothing by the excluded authors was used.
     4	
     5	Throughout, $p$ denotes a prime, $c_0:=-4\zeta(-1/2)$, and
     6	$$A_p=1-\tfrac3{p^2}+\tfrac2{p^3},\quad B_p=\tfrac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3},\quad D_p=\tfrac{(p-1)^2(p+1)}{p^3}.$$
     7	Then $h(q)=c_0\prod_p a_p(v_p(q))$ with $a_p(0)=A_p$, $a_p(1)=B_p$, $a_p(v)=D_p$ for $v\ge2$. Write $f(t)=a\,t^d+\dots$ with $a\ge1$.
     8	
     9	## 0. Preliminaries
    10	
    11	**Sign of $c_0$.** By the functional equation $\zeta(s)=2^s\pi^{s-1}\sin(\pi s/2)\Gamma(1-s)\zeta(1-s)$ at $s=-1/2$:
    12	$\zeta(-1/2)=2^{-1/2}\pi^{-3/2}\sin(-\pi/4)\Gamma(3/2)\zeta(3/2)=-\zeta(3/2)/(4\pi)<0$, since $\zeta(3/2)>0$. So $c_0=\zeta(3/2)/\pi>0$. (Numerically $\zeta(-1/2)=-0.2078862\ldots$, matching $-\zeta(3/2)/(4\pi)$; checked with mpmath.)
    13	
    14	**Elementary identities** (verified symbolically with sympy, and by hand):
    15	$$A_p=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3},\qquad B_p-A_p=-\frac1p+p^{-3/2}+p^{-2}-p^{-5/2},\qquad D_p-B_p=-p^{-3/2}(1-p^{-1/2})(1-p^{-1}).$$
    16	Consequently, for all primes $p$:
    17	
    18	* $A_p,B_p,D_p>0$ (for $B_p$: $p^2-2+\sqrt p>0$). Also $A_2=\frac12$ and $A_p\ge 1-3/p^2\ge\frac23$ for $p\ge3$, so $A_p\ge\frac12$, and $0<1-A_p\le 3/p^2$.
    19	* $|B_p-A_p|\le 1/p$, because $-1/p+p^{-3/2}\in(-1/p,0)$ and $p^{-2}-p^{-5/2}\in[0,p^{-2})$.
    20	* $-p^{-3/2}<D_p-B_p<0$.
    21	
    22	**The function $\rho$.** By the Chinese remainder theorem $\rho$ is multiplicative. Let $P_0$ be the finite set of primes dividing the content of $f$.
    23	
    24	* For $p\notin P_0$, $f\bmod p$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree $\le d$, so $\rho(p)\le d$.
    25	* Every root mod $p$ has exactly $p$ lifts mod $p^2$, so $\rho(p^2)\le p\rho(p)$ for all $p$.

    82	$$\sum_{e>E}\frac{|u(e)|\rho(e)}{e}\le E^{-1/2}C_1\sum_{a,b\text{ sqfree}}(2d)^{\omega(a)+\omega(b)}a^{-3/2}b^{-3/2}=E^{-1/2}C_1\Bigl(\prod_p\bigl(1+2dp^{-3/2}\bigr)\Bigr)^2=:c_4E^{-1/2}.\tag{3.5}$$
    83	In particular $\sum_e|u(e)|\rho(e)/e<\infty$.
    84	
    85	**(ii) Short sum.** Using $(2d)^{\omega(n)}\le C_\varepsilon n^\varepsilon$ and (3.4),
    86	$$\sum_{e\le E}|u(e)|\rho(e)\le C_1C_\varepsilon E^{\varepsilon}\sum_{a\le E}\frac1a\sum_{b\le E^{1/2}}b^{-1/2}\le C_1C_\varepsilon E^\varepsilon(1+\log E)\cdot2E^{1/4}\ll_{f,\varepsilon}E^{1/4+2\varepsilon}.\tag{3.6}$$
    87	
    88	**(iii) Euler product.** The multiplicative function $e\mapsto u(e)\rho(e)/e$ has absolutely convergent sum by (3.5). So
    89	$$\sum_e\frac{u(e)\rho(e)}{e}=\prod_p\Bigl(1+u(p)x_p+u(p^2)z_p\Bigr).$$
    90	Now $1+u(p)x_p+u(p^2)z_p=1+\frac{B_p-A_p}{A_p}x_p+\frac{D_p-B_p}{A_p}z_p=\tau_p/A_p$ by the second formula for $\tau_p$ in §1. Hence
    91	$$\sum_e\frac{u(e)\rho(e)}e=\prod_p\frac{\tau_p}{A_p}=\frac1A\prod_p\tau_p.\tag{3.7}$$
    92	(The product converges as $\prod\tau_p$ and $\prod A_p$ both converge absolutely and are nonzero.)
    93	
    94	### 3.3 Truncation of the divisor sum
    95	
    96	Take $E=y$ and write $b(f(k))=\sum_{e\mid f(k),\,e\le y}u(e)+T_k$ with $T_k=\sum_{e\mid f(k),\,e>y}u(e)$. By (3.2), for $e>y$, $|u(e)|\le 4^{\omega(e)}y^{-3/4}$. Since $4^{\omega(e)}\le\tau(e)^2$, we have $\sum_{e\mid n}4^{\omega(e)}\le\tau(n)^3\le C_\varepsilon n^{\varepsilon}$. Thus
    97	$$|T_k|\le y^{-3/4}C_\varepsilon f(k)^\varepsilon\le C_\varepsilon y^{-3/4}Y^\varepsilon\quad(k\le y;\ f\text{ increasing}).$$
    98	By (0.1), $\sum_{k\le y}F(k)\le yc_3F(y)\le c_5Y^{3/2}$ (using $F(y)\ll Y^{3/2}/y$). So
    99	$$\Bigl|\sum_{k\le y}F(k)T_k\Bigr|\le C_\varepsilon c_5\,Y^{3/2+\varepsilon}y^{-3/4}.\tag{3.8}$$
   100	(This is stronger than needed since $y^{-3/4}\le y^{-1/2}$.)
   101	
   102	### 3.4 Counting in residue classes
   103	
   104	For $e\le y$ let $N(e)=\sum_{k\le y,\ e\mid f(k)}F(k)=\sum_{r\bmod e,\ f(r)\equiv0}\ \sum_{1\le k\le y,\ k\equiv r(e)}F(k)$, a sum over $\rho(e)$ classes.
   105	
   106	**Lemma.** Let $G\ge 0$ be monotone on an interval $I=(\alpha,\beta]$ and let $k_1<\dots<k_n$ be the points of $I$ in a fixed residue class mod $e$. Then $|\sum_jG(k_j)-\frac1e\int_IG|\le3\sup_IG$.
   107	
   108	*Proof.* If $G$ is nonincreasing, then $G(k_{j+1})\le\frac1e\int_{k_j}^{k_{j+1}}G\le G(k_j)$. Summing over $j<n$ gives $\sum_{j}G(k_j)-G(k_1)\le\frac1e\int_{k_1}^{k_n}G\le\sum_jG(k_j)-G(k_n)$. So $|\sum_jG(k_j)-\frac1e\int_{k_1}^{k_n}G|\le\sup G$. The remaining pieces $(\alpha,k_1]$, $(k_n,\beta]$ have length $\le e$, so contribute $\le\sup G$ each to $\frac1e\int$. If $n=0$, then $|I|\le e$ and $\frac1e\int_IG\le\sup G$. The nondecreasing case is symmetric. $\square$
   109	
   110	Split $[1,y]$ into at most $2d-1$ intervals of monotonicity of $F$ (§0), made half-open so that each integer lies in exactly one. The first interval is closed, which only adds the point $1$, handled identically by treating $[1,\beta]$ as $(1-\delta,\beta]$ with $\delta<1$. By the Lemma, for each residue class,
   111	$$\Bigl|\sum_{k\le y,\ k\equiv r(e)}F(k)-\frac1e\int_1^yF\Bigr|\le3(2d-1)\sup_{[1,y]}F\le3(2d-1)c_3F(y).$$
   112	Summing over the $\rho(e)$ classes,
   113	$$N(e)=\frac{\rho(e)}e\cdot\frac23\bigl(Y^{3/2}-f(1)^{3/2}\bigr)+\theta_e\,6d\,c_3\rho(e)F(y),\qquad|\theta_e|\le1.\tag{3.9}$$
   114	
   115	### 3.5 Assembly
   116	
   117	Since $S=\sum_{e\le y}u(e)N(e)+\sum_{k\le y}F(k)T_k$, (3.9) gives
   118	$$S=\tfrac23\bigl(Y^{3/2}-f(1)^{3/2}\bigr)\sum_{e\le y}\frac{u(e)\rho(e)}e+O\Bigl(F(y)\sum_{e\le y}|u(e)|\rho(e)\Bigr)+O\bigl(Y^{3/2+\varepsilon}y^{-3/4}\bigr).$$
   119	By (3.7) and (3.5) with $E=y$: $\sum_{e\le y}u(e)\rho(e)/e=A^{-1}\prod_p\tau_p+O(y^{-1/2})$. The sum $\sum_{e\le y}u(e)\rho(e)/e$ is bounded by a constant. By (3.6) with $E=y$ and $F(y)\ll Y^{3/2}/y$, the middle error is $\ll Y^{3/2}y^{-1}y^{1/4+2\varepsilon}=Y^{3/2}y^{-3/4+2\varepsilon}$. Hence
   120	$$S=\frac{2}{3A}\Bigl(\prod_p\tau_p\Bigr)Y^{3/2}+O\bigl(Y^{3/2}y^{-1/2}\bigr)+O(1)+O\bigl(Y^{3/2}y^{-3/4+2\varepsilon}\bigr)+O\bigl(Y^{3/2+\varepsilon}y^{-3/4}\bigr).$$
   121	The $O(1)$ term arises from $f(1)^{3/2}$ times a bounded sum. It is $\ll Y^{3/2}y^{-1/2}$ because $Y^{3/2}\ge c_1^{3/2}y^{3d/2}$ and $3d/2-1/2\ge1$. Taking $\varepsilon$ small (replace $2\varepsilon$ by $\varepsilon'$) and using $y^{-3/4+\varepsilon'}\le y^{-1/2}$ for $\varepsilon'\le1/4$ (all remaining errors are then $\ll Y^{3/2+\varepsilon}y^{-1/2}$; for larger $\varepsilon$ the claim follows from the claim for smaller $\varepsilon$ since $Y\ge 2$):
   122	$$S=\frac{2}{3A}\Bigl(\prod_p\tau_p\Bigr)Y^{3/2}+O_{f,\varepsilon}\bigl(Y^{3/2+\varepsilon}y^{-1/2}\bigr).$$
   123	Multiplying by $c_0A$:
   124	$$\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))=\tfrac23c_0\Bigl(\prod_p\tau_p\Bigr)Y^{3/2}+O\bigl(Y^{3/2+\varepsilon}y^{-1/2}\bigr)=C_fY^{3/2}+O_{f,\varepsilon}\bigl(Y^{3/2+\varepsilon}y^{-1/2}\bigr).\qquad\blacksquare$$
   125	
   126	All implied constants depend only on $f$ and $\varepsilon$ (through $d$, $c_1,c_2$, $C_1$, $f(1)$, $C_\varepsilon$).
   127	
   128	## 4. Numerical sanity checks (Python)
   129	
   130	* sympy confirmed the identities for $A_p$, $B_p-A_p$ and $D_p-B_p$ in §0.
   131	* mpmath confirmed $\zeta(-1/2)=-\zeta(3/2)/(4\pi)=-0.2078862\ldots$.
   132	* A direct computation of $\sum_{k\le2000}F(k)h(f(k))$ against $C_fY^{3/2}$ for $f=t^2+1$ gave $1.10576\times10^9$ vs $1.10482\times10^9$. For $f=t+1$ it gave $11505.97$ vs $11501.80$. Both agree to $\approx10^{-3}$. The check truncates the Euler products at $p\le3000$ and approximates $\rho(p^2)\approx\rho(p)/p$, which is exact for these squarefree $f$ at large $p$.

1	# Proof of P5: sawtooth sums $B(Z/t^2)$ with multiplicative weights
     2	
     3	No external result is used except the classical analytic continuation of $\zeta$ (derived below from Euler–Maclaurin, cf. Montgomery–Vaughan, *Multiplicative Number Theory I* (2007), Thm. B.5 and §1.3) and the bound $2^{\omega(q)}\ll_\varepsilon q^\varepsilon$. Nothing from the excluded sources was used.
     4	
     5	Notation: $B(u)=\{u\}(1-\{u\})\in[0,\tfrac14]$ (1-periodic, continuous); $\psi(u)=\{u\}-\tfrac12$; $\psi_2(u)=\tfrac12(\{u\}^2-\{u\})+\tfrac1{12}=\tfrac1{12}-\tfrac12B(u)$. Then $\psi_2$ is continuous, 1-periodic, $\psi_2'=\psi$ off the integers, $|\psi_2|\le\frac1{12}$, $\psi_2(n)=\frac1{12}$ for $n\in\mathbb Z$, and $|\psi|\le\frac12$, $\psi(n)=-\frac12$.
     6	
     7	## 0. Euler–Maclaurin in the form used
     8	
     9	**Lemma EM.** Let $a<b$ be reals, $F\in C^2[a,b]$. Then
    10	$$\sum_{a<n\le b}F(n)=\int_a^bF\,du+\psi(a)F(a)-\psi(b)F(b)-\psi_2(a)F'(a)+\psi_2(b)F'(b)-\int_a^b\psi_2(u)F''(u)\,du .$$
    11	*Proof.* $\lfloor u\rfloor=u-\frac12-\psi(u)$, so $\sum_{a<n\le b}F(n)=\int_{(a,b]}F\,d\lfloor u\rfloor=\int_a^bF\,du-\int_{(a,b]}F\,d\psi$. As $\psi$ is right-continuous of bounded variation and $F$ is continuous, $\int_{(a,b]}F\,d\psi=F(b)\psi(b)-F(a)\psi(a)-\int_a^b\psi F'\,du$. Finally $\int_a^b\psi F'=[\psi_2F']_a^b-\int_a^b\psi_2F''$. $\square$ (Check: $F\equiv1$ gives $\lfloor b\rfloor-\lfloor a\rfloor$.) If $b=\infty$ and $F,F'\to0$, $F''\in L^1$, the same holds with the terms at $b$ dropped.
    12	
    13	## (a) The value of $I$
    14	
    15	Substituting $v=u^{-2}$, $du=-\frac12v^{-3/2}dv$ gives $I=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}dv$. This converges: $B(v)\le v$ near $0$ and $B\le\frac14$, $\int^\infty v^{-3/2}<\infty$ at infinity. So $I$ is finite and the first equality holds.
    16	
    17	*Value.* $B$ is continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with $B'(v)=1-2\{v\}$. Integrating by parts on $[0,X]$,
    18	$\int_0^XB\,v^{-3/2}dv=[-2Bv^{-1/2}]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'v^{-1/2}dv$. The boundary term tends to $0$ ($B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ at $0$; $\le\frac12X^{-1/2}$ at $X$). Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}=2\lim_N\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}dv$ ($N\in\mathbb N$), the limit existing since the integral on the left converges.
    19	On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$, $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$,
    20	$$\int_n^{n+1}B'v^{-1/2}dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}dv .$$
    21	Summing over $0\le n\le N-1$:
    22	$$\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^{N}m^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.$$
    23	Now apply Lemma EM on $(N,\infty)$ with $F(u)=u^{-s}$, $\sigma>1$ (with $\psi(N)=-\frac12,\ \psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$):
    24	$$\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac{s}{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}du.$$
    25	The right side is analytic in $\sigma>-1$, $s\neq1$; by analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}+\text{RHS}$ there. At $s=-\frac12$ (where $s(s+1)=-\frac14$, and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}du|\le\frac1{12}\cdot2N^{-1/2}$):
    26	$$\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).$$
    27	Inserting: $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}dv=-4\zeta(-\frac12)-\frac83N^{3/2}-2N^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\frac83N^{3/2}+O(N^{-1/2})\to-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
    28	Therefore $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$.
    29	
    30	*Numerical check (Python/mpmath):* $-4\zeta(-1/2)=0.8315448999\ldots$ (matches the stated value), and $\frac12\int_0^{400}B(v)v^{-3/2}dv=0.82321$, with tail $\approx\frac12\cdot\frac16\cdot2\cdot400^{-1/2}=0.00833$, total $0.83154$. $\square$
    31	
    32	Also, for $Z>0$, $u=\sqrt Z\,w$ gives
    33	$$\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z.\tag{0.1}$$
    34	
    35	## (b) $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$
    36	
    37	I show this with $c_1=60$.
    38	
    39	**Case $Z<1$.** $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z\le2Z^{1/3}$, and $0<I\sqrt Z\le IZ^{1/3}<Z^{1/3}$ ($I<1$). The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.
    40	
    41	**Case $Z\ge1$.** Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$, $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Since $T+1>\Lambda$ and $T+1\le2T$, we have $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
    42	$$\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad\frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda.\tag{b.1}$$
    43	(Indeed $Z/T^3<\Lambda^3/(\Lambda/2)^3=8$; $Z/T^2<\Lambda^3/(\Lambda^2/4)=4\Lambda$; $Z^2/T^5<\Lambda^6\cdot32/\Lambda^5$.)
    44	
    45	*Small $s$.* $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)\le T/4\le\Lambda/4$ and by (0.1) $0\le\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)du\le T/4\le\Lambda/4$. So it suffices to show
    46	$$\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)du\Bigr|\le 57\Lambda,\tag{b.2}$$
    47	which gives $|\sum_sB(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z|\le57\Lambda+\Lambda/2\le60\Lambda$.
    48	
    49	*Decomposition.* For real $x\ge0$ with $m=\lfloor x\rfloor$: $B(x)=(x-m)(1-x+m)=x-x^2+2mx-m-m^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^{m}2(x-k)=2mx-m^2-m$. Hence
    50	$$B(x)=x-x^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(x-k)_+,\qquad(y)_+=\max(y,0).$$
    51	Put $A(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$. Then $B(Z/u^2)=A(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only $k<K_0$ contribute ($G_k(u)\le(Z/T^2-k)_+$), so at most $K_0<4\Lambda$ values of $k$ occur. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ for $T\le u\le R_k:=\sqrt{Z/k}$ (note $R_k>T$) and $0$ beyond.
    52	
    53	*Apply Lemma EM.* With $F=A$ on $(T,\infty)$ and with $F=Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$, using $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$, $G_k(R_k)=0$, and adding (the $k$-sum is finite):
    54	$$\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)du+E_1+E_2+E_3+E_4+E_5,$$
    55	where (writing $G_k'$, $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$)
    56	
    57	* $E_1=\psi(T)\bigl[A(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$, by the decomposition at $u=T$. **This is the one place where cancellation is essential:** the individual terms are of size $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $\le\frac12\cdot\frac14$. So $|E_1|\le\frac18$.
    58	* $E_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[A'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$. Here $A'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$, $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By (b.1), $|A'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$, $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<4\cdot4\Lambda\cdot8=128\Lambda$. So $|E_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
    59	* $E_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2A''du$, $A''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$, so $|E_3|\le\frac1{12}\bigl(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5\bigr)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
    60	* $E_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''du$, with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Z/u^4\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|E_4|\le2\cdot\frac1{12}\cdot K_0\cdot16<\frac2{12}\cdot4\Lambda\cdot16=\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
    61	* $E_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$, $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<K_0<4\Lambda$: $k^{3/2}<8\Lambda^{3/2}$, so $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}=32\Lambda^{5/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$: $|E_5|\le2\cdot\frac1{12}\cdot2\cdot\frac{32\Lambda^{5/2}}{\Lambda^{3/2}}=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. (This is the kink of $G_k$ at $R_k$; summing over $K_0\ll Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is exactly what produces the exponent $\frac13$.)
    62	
    63	Also $\int_T^\infty G_k=\int_T^{R_k}G_k$ and $\sum_k$ over $k\ge K_0$ gives $0$, so $\int_T^\infty[A+2\sum_kG_k]=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)du$ (all integrals converge absolutely).
    64	
    65	Total: $|E_1|+\dots+|E_5|\le\Lambda\bigl(\tfrac18+\tfrac{272}{12}+12+\tfrac{32}3+\tfrac{32}3\bigr)<57\Lambda$ (using $\Lambda\ge1$ for $E_1$): $0.125+22.67+12+10.67+10.67=56.1$. This is (b.2). $\square$
    66	
    67	*Numerical check:* $(\sum_sB(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z)/Z^{1/3}$ for $Z=1.5,\,10,\dots,10^7$ lies in $[-0.16,0.02]$.
    68	
    69	## (c) Weighted version
    70	
    71	Fix $q\in\mathbb N$ and put $f(t)=\kappa(t)\mathbf 1_{(t,q)=1}$. It is multiplicative with $f(p)=\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ for $p\nmid q$, $f(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$, and $f(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. In particular $0\le f\le C_0:=\prod_p(1+\frac2{p^2-2})<\infty$.
    72	
    73	**Convolution.** Let $b=\mu*f$, i.e. $f=1*b$. $b$ is multiplicative, with $b(p^j)=f(p^j)-f(p^{j-1})$:
    74	* $p\mid q$: $b(p)=-1$, $b(p^j)=0$ ($j\ge2$);
    75	* $p\nmid q$: $b(p)=\frac{2}{p^2-2}$, $b(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$, $b(p^j)=0$ ($j\ge3$).
    76	
    77	*Absolute convergence.* $\sum_d|b(d)|d^{-\alpha}=\prod_p\bigl(1+\sum_{j}|b(p^j)|p^{-j\alpha}\bigr)$. For $\alpha=\frac23$:
    78	$$\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_d\frac{|b(d)|}{d^{2/3}}=\prod_{p\mid q}(1+p^{-2/3})\prod_{p\nmid q}\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}p^{-4/3}\Bigr).$$
    79	For $p\nmid q$ the factor is $\le1+\frac{2}{p^2-2}p^{-2/3}+2p^{-4/3}$ (as $\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}\le2$), and $\sum_pp^{-4/3}<\infty$, $\sum_p\frac1{p^2-2}<\infty$. Hence the product over $p\nmid q$ is bounded by an absolute constant $C_1$ (independent of $q$), and
    80	$$\Sigma_{2/3}\le C_1\prod_{p\mid q}(1+p^{-2/3})\le C_1\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C(\varepsilon)\,q^{\varepsilon}$$

    18	$\int_0^XB\,v^{-3/2}dv=[-2Bv^{-1/2}]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'v^{-1/2}dv$. The boundary term tends to $0$ ($B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ at $0$; $\le\frac12X^{-1/2}$ at $X$). Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}=2\lim_N\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}dv$ ($N\in\mathbb N$), the limit existing since the integral on the left converges.
    19	On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$, $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$,
    20	$$\int_n^{n+1}B'v^{-1/2}dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}dv .$$
    21	Summing over $0\le n\le N-1$:
    22	$$\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^{N}m^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.$$
    23	Now apply Lemma EM on $(N,\infty)$ with $F(u)=u^{-s}$, $\sigma>1$ (with $\psi(N)=-\frac12,\ \psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$):
    24	$$\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac{s}{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}du.$$
    25	The right side is analytic in $\sigma>-1$, $s\neq1$; by analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}+\text{RHS}$ there. At $s=-\frac12$ (where $s(s+1)=-\frac14$, and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}du|\le\frac1{12}\cdot2N^{-1/2}$):
    26	$$\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).$$
    27	Inserting: $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}dv=-4\zeta(-\frac12)-\frac83N^{3/2}-2N^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\frac83N^{3/2}+O(N^{-1/2})\to-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
    28	Therefore $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$.
    29	
    30	*Numerical check (Python/mpmath):* $-4\zeta(-1/2)=0.8315448999\ldots$ (matches the stated value), and $\frac12\int_0^{400}B(v)v^{-3/2}dv=0.82321$, with tail $\approx\frac12\cdot\frac16\cdot2\cdot400^{-1/2}=0.00833$, total $0.83154$. $\square$
    31	
    32	Also, for $Z>0$, $u=\sqrt Z\,w$ gives
    33	$$\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z.\tag{0.1}$$
    34	
    35	## (b) $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$
    36	
    37	I show this with $c_1=60$.
    38	
    39	**Case $Z<1$.** $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z\le2Z^{1/3}$, and $0<I\sqrt Z\le IZ^{1/3}<Z^{1/3}$ ($I<1$). The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.
    40	
    41	**Case $Z\ge1$.** Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$, $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Since $T+1>\Lambda$ and $T+1\le2T$, we have $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
    42	$$\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad\frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda.\tag{b.1}$$
    43	(Indeed $Z/T^3<\Lambda^3/(\Lambda/2)^3=8$; $Z/T^2<\Lambda^3/(\Lambda^2/4)=4\Lambda$; $Z^2/T^5<\Lambda^6\cdot32/\Lambda^5$.)
    44	
    45	*Small $s$.* $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)\le T/4\le\Lambda/4$ and by (0.1) $0\le\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)du\le T/4\le\Lambda/4$. So it suffices to show
    46	$$\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)du\Bigr|\le 57\Lambda,\tag{b.2}$$
    47	which gives $|\sum_sB(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z|\le57\Lambda+\Lambda/2\le60\Lambda$.
    48	
    49	*Decomposition.* For real $x\ge0$ with $m=\lfloor x\rfloor$: $B(x)=(x-m)(1-x+m)=x-x^2+2mx-m-m^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^{m}2(x-k)=2mx-m^2-m$. Hence
    50	$$B(x)=x-x^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(x-k)_+,\qquad(y)_+=\max(y,0).$$
    51	Put $A(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$. Then $B(Z/u^2)=A(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only $k<K_0$ contribute ($G_k(u)\le(Z/T^2-k)_+$), so at most $K_0<4\Lambda$ values of $k$ occur. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ for $T\le u\le R_k:=\sqrt{Z/k}$ (note $R_k>T$) and $0$ beyond.
    52	
    53	*Apply Lemma EM.* With $F=A$ on $(T,\infty)$ and with $F=Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$, using $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$, $G_k(R_k)=0$, and adding (the $k$-sum is finite):
    54	$$\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)du+E_1+E_2+E_3+E_4+E_5,$$
    55	where (writing $G_k'$, $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$)
    56	
    57	* $E_1=\psi(T)\bigl[A(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$, by the decomposition at $u=T$. **This is the one place where cancellation is essential:** the individual terms are of size $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $\le\frac12\cdot\frac14$. So $|E_1|\le\frac18$.
    58	* $E_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[A'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$. Here $A'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$, $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By (b.1), $|A'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$, $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<4\cdot4\Lambda\cdot8=128\Lambda$. So $|E_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
    59	* $E_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2A''du$, $A''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$, so $|E_3|\le\frac1{12}\bigl(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5\bigr)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
    60	* $E_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''du$, with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Z/u^4\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|E_4|\le2\cdot\frac1{12}\cdot K_0\cdot16<\frac2{12}\cdot4\Lambda\cdot16=\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
    61	* $E_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$, $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<K_0<4\Lambda$: $k^{3/2}<8\Lambda^{3/2}$, so $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}=32\Lambda^{5/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$: $|E_5|\le2\cdot\frac1{12}\cdot2\cdot\frac{32\Lambda^{5/2}}{\Lambda^{3/2}}=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. (This is the kink of $G_k$ at $R_k$; summing over $K_0\ll Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is exactly what produces the exponent $\frac13$.)
    62	
    63	Also $\int_T^\infty G_k=\int_T^{R_k}G_k$ and $\sum_k$ over $k\ge K_0$ gives $0$, so $\int_T^\infty[A+2\sum_kG_k]=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)du$ (all integrals converge absolutely).
    64	
    65	Total: $|E_1|+\dots+|E_5|\le\Lambda\bigl(\tfrac18+\tfrac{272}{12}+12+\tfrac{32}3+\tfrac{32}3\bigr)<57\Lambda$ (using $\Lambda\ge1$ for $E_1$): $0.125+22.67+12+10.67+10.67=56.1$. This is (b.2). $\square$
    66	
    67	*Numerical check:* $(\sum_sB(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z)/Z^{1/3}$ for $Z=1.5,\,10,\dots,10^7$ lies in $[-0.16,0.02]$.
    68	
    69	## (c) Weighted version
    70	
    71	Fix $q\in\mathbb N$ and put $f(t)=\kappa(t)\mathbf 1_{(t,q)=1}$. It is multiplicative with $f(p)=\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ for $p\nmid q$, $f(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$, and $f(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. In particular $0\le f\le C_0:=\prod_p(1+\frac2{p^2-2})<\infty$.
    72	
    73	**Convolution.** Let $b=\mu*f$, i.e. $f=1*b$. $b$ is multiplicative, with $b(p^j)=f(p^j)-f(p^{j-1})$:
    74	* $p\mid q$: $b(p)=-1$, $b(p^j)=0$ ($j\ge2$);
    75	* $p\nmid q$: $b(p)=\frac{2}{p^2-2}$, $b(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$, $b(p^j)=0$ ($j\ge3$).
    76	
    77	*Absolute convergence.* $\sum_d|b(d)|d^{-\alpha}=\prod_p\bigl(1+\sum_{j}|b(p^j)|p^{-j\alpha}\bigr)$. For $\alpha=\frac23$:
    78	$$\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_d\frac{|b(d)|}{d^{2/3}}=\prod_{p\mid q}(1+p^{-2/3})\prod_{p\nmid q}\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}p^{-4/3}\Bigr).$$
    79	For $p\nmid q$ the factor is $\le1+\frac{2}{p^2-2}p^{-2/3}+2p^{-4/3}$ (as $\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}\le2$), and $\sum_pp^{-4/3}<\infty$, $\sum_p\frac1{p^2-2}<\infty$. Hence the product over $p\nmid q$ is bounded by an absolute constant $C_1$ (independent of $q$), and
    80	$$\Sigma_{2/3}\le C_1\prod_{p\mid q}(1+p^{-2/3})\le C_1\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C(\varepsilon)\,q^{\varepsilon}$$

    if isinstance(d,dict): return {k:strip(v) for k,v in d.items() if 'runtime' not in k and k!='seconds'}

    arch=[round(r['normalised'],6) for r in prim]
    print(p,len(rows),len(nums),len(arch), max(abs(u-v) for u,v in zip(nums,arch)))
    print(' keys',list(a['polynomials'][p].keys()))
EOF

import json,sys,numpy as np
a=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
for p in ['k^2+1','k^3+2','2k+1']:
    rows=a['polynomials'][p]['rows']
    X=max(r['x'] for r in rows)
    R=[r for r in rows if r['x']==X and r['ratio_target']>=0.01]
    rr=np.array([r['ratio_actual'] for r in R]); N=np.array([r['V']/(r['x']**0.5*r['fy']**1.5) for r in R])
    M=np.vstack([np.ones_like(rr),np.sqrt(rr),rr]).T
    c=np.linalg.lstsq(M,N,rcond=None)[0]
    # fixed ratio slopes
    sl=[]

def euler_constant(name, P):
    """Partial values (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p and a rigorous interval for
    the full product (tail bound of Section 10.2)."""
    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
    xp, zp = r1 / P, r2 / (P.astype(np.float64) ** 2)
    a_m1, ba, cb = local_factors(P)
    s_m1 = a_m1 + ba * xp + cb * zp                                   # sigma_p - 1
    if np.any(1 + s_m1 <= 0):
        raise RuntimeError('nonpositive local factor')
    logs = np.log1p(s_m1)
    pref = 2 * float(I_CONST) / 3
    partial = {}
    for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS:
        partial[N] = pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N]))
    d = POLY[name][2]
    K = 3 + 2 * d
    N = PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]
    # |log prod_{p>N} sigma_p| <= K/(1-K/N^2) * sum_{p>N} p^-2, and every prime
    # p > N >= 30 lies in one of 8 classes mod 30, each contributing at most
    # N^-2 + 1/(30N).
    tail = K / (1 - K / N ** 2) * 8 * (1 / N ** 2 + 1 / (30 * N))
    val = partial[N]
    return dict(partial=partial, value=val, lower=val * math.exp(-tail),
                upper=val * math.exp(tail), tail_log_bound=tail, K=K)


def vaughan_c2(P):
    """c_2 = 8 C_1 (-zeta(-1/2)) / (3 zeta(2)^2), Vaughan (2005), (1.14)-(1.15)
    with k = 2; C_1 truncated to p <= N."""
    p = P.astype(np.float64)
    term = ((p - 1) ** 2 * p ** 1.5 - 2 * p ** 4 + 3 * p ** 3 - p) / (p ** 2 * (p ** 2 - 1) ** 2)
    logs = np.log1p(term)
    pref = float(8 * (-mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / (3 * mp.zeta(2) ** 2))
    return {N: pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N])) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS}


def round_out(v, nd, up):
    """Round the float v to nd decimals, downwards (up=False) or upwards (up=True).
    Used for interval endpoints, so that the printed interval contains the
    computed one."""
    q = Decimal(1).scaleb(-nd)
    return Decimal(v).quantize(q, rounding=ROUND_CEILING if up else ROUND_FLOOR)


def certified_digits(lower, upper, maxdigits=12):
    """Longest decimal truncation shared by every number in [lower, upper]
    (0 < lower <= upper < 1); these digits are fixed by the interval."""
    best = None
    for nd in range(1, maxdigits + 1):
        a = round_out(lower, nd, False)
        b = round_out(upper, nd, False)
        if a != b:
            break
        best = a
    return str(best)


def euler_float_check(name, N=10 ** 5, dps=40):
    """Recompute (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p with mpmath at dps digits, to
    gauge the floating-point rounding of euler_constant (not a certification)."""
    P = primes_upto(N)
    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
    with mp.workdps(dps):
        tot = mp.mpf(0)
        for p, a1, a2 in zip(P.tolist(), r1.tolist(), r2.tolist()):
            p = mp.mpf(p)
            a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
            b = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + mp.sqrt(p)) / p ** 3
            c = (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
            xp, zp = mp.mpf(int(a1)) / p, mp.mpf(int(a2)) / p ** 2
            tot += mp.log(a * (1 - xp) + b * (xp - zp) + c * zp)
        return 2 * (-4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / 3 * mp.exp(tot)


def eligibility(results, name):
    """For the rows at the largest x: the largest delta for which the row lies in
    the range x^(7/9+delta) <= f(y) <= x^(1-delta) of Theorem 1.1(iii), computed
    from the actual ratio f(y)/x (negative: outside the range for every delta)."""
    rows = all_rows(results, name)
    xl = max(r['x'] for r in rows)
    out = []
    for r in sorted([r for r in rows if r['x'] == xl], key=lambda r: r['ratio_target']):
        lr = math.log(r['fy']) / math.log(xl)
        out.append(dict(x=xl, ratio_target=r['ratio_target'], ratio_actual=r['ratio_actual'],
                        delta_max=min(lr - 7 / 9, 1 - lr)))
    return out

def write(path, text):
    path.write_text(text)
    return str(path.relative_to(HERE))


def make_outputs(results, compare, consts, c2, shape, selftest, symb, rho_checked, elapsed, floatcheck, elig):
    GEN.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    arts = []
    # Table: constants
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{l' + 'r' * len(PRIME_CUTOFFS) + 'l}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & ' + ' & '.join(f'$N=10^{{{int(math.log10(N))}}}$' for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS)
             + r' & interval for $C_f$ \\', r'\midrule']
    for name in NAMES + ['t']:
        c = consts[name]
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + ' & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(c['partial'][N], 9) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS)
                     + f" & $[{round_out(c['lower'], 9, False)},\\,{round_out(c['upper'], 9, True)}]$ \\\\")
    lines.append(r'Vaughan $c_2$ & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(c2[N], 9) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS) + r' & \\')
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_constants.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: largest-x normalised values and stability
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{l' + 'r' * (len(RATIOS) + 1) + '}', r'\toprule',
             r'$r$ & $0.005$ & ' + ' & '.join(f'${r:g}$' for r in RATIOS) + r' \\', r'\midrule']
    for name in NAMES:
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        xs = sorted({r['x'] for r in p['rows']})
        xl = xs[-1]
        last = {r['ratio_target']: r for r in all_rows(results, name) if r['x'] == xl}
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + ' & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(last[r]['normalised'], 5) for r in [.005] + RATIOS) + r' \\')
        st = {s['ratio']: s['relative_change'] for s in p['stability']}
        dst = {s['ratio']: s['relative_change'] for s in p['diagnostic_stability']}
        ch = [dst.get(.005)] + [st[r] for r in RATIOS]
        lines.append(r'\quad change (\%) & ' + ' & '.join(f'${100 * c:+.4f}$' for c in ch) + r' \\')
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_largest.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: fits versus C_f
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & $\alpha+\beta$ (fixed $r$) & $\beta$ (fixed $x$) & $C_{\mathrm{extr}}\pm$ envelope & $C_f$ & $\frac{C_{\mathrm{extr}}-C_f}{C_f}$ & in envelopes \\',
             r'\midrule']
    fitsum = {}
    for name in NAMES:
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        fr, fx, ce = p['fit_fixed_ratio'], p['fit_fixed_x'], p['constant_extrapolated']
        Cf = consts[name]['value']
        rel = (ce['value'] - Cf) / Cf
        units = (ce['value'] - Cf) / ce['uncertainty']
        fitsum[name] = dict(alpha_plus_beta=fr['alpha_plus_beta'], alpha_plus_beta_se=fr['se'],
                            beta_fixed_x=fx['beta'], beta_se=fx['beta_se'], C_extrapolated=ce['value'],
                            envelope=ce['uncertainty'], C_f=Cf, relative_difference=rel,
                            difference_in_envelopes=units,
                            fit_coefficients=ce['primary_fit']['coefficients'],
                            cutoff_fits={str(v['ratio_cutoff']): v['value'] for v in ce['cutoff_fits']},
                            alternative_models={v['model']: v['value'] for v in ce['alternative_models']},
                            upper_window_fits={str(v['upper_ratio']): v['value'] for v in ce['upper_ratio_window_fits']},
                            previous_x_fit=ce['previous_x_fit']['value'],
                            joint_fit={k: p['fit_joint'][k] for k in ['alpha', 'alpha_se', 'beta', 'beta_se', 'C']})
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + f" & ${fr['alpha_plus_beta']:.4f}\\pm{fr['se']:.4f}$ & ${fx['beta']:.3f}\\pm{fx['beta_se']:.3f}$"
                     f" & ${ce['value']:.4f}\\pm{ce['uncertainty']:.4f}$ & ${Cf:.5f}$ & ${100 * rel:+.2f}\\%$ & ${units:+.2f}$ \\\\")
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_fits.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: model sensitivity of the extrapolation
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & primary & $C+a\sqrt r$ & $+\,r^{3/2}$ & $r\le 0.1$ & cutoff $0.005$ & previous $x$ \\', r'\midrule']
    for name in NAMES:
        fs = fitsum[name]
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + f" & {fs['C_extrapolated']:.5f} & {fs['alternative_models']['sqrt']:.5f}"
                     f" & {fs['alternative_models']['sqrt+linear+threehalves']:.5f} & {fs['upper_window_fits']['0.1']:.5f}"
                     f" & {fs['cutoff_fits']['0.005']:.5f} & {fs['previous_x_fit']:.5f} \\\\")
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_sensitivity.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: exact shape
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{llrrrrrr}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & $x$ & $r$ & $y$ & $N_{\mathrm{data}}$ & $N_{\mathrm{MT}}$ & $V_f/\Sigma_{\mathrm{MT}}$ & $N_h$ \\', r'\midrule']
    prev = None
    for row in shape:
        if row['ratio_target'] not in (.005, .01, .1, 1.):
            continue
        key = (row['poly'], row['x'])
        if prev is not None and key[0] != prev[0]:
            lines.append(r'\midrule')
        lab = TEXNAME[row['poly']] if (prev is None or key[0] != prev[0]) else ''
        xl = sci(row['x']) if key != prev else ''
        prev = key
        lines.append(f"{lab} & {xl} & ${row['ratio_target']:g}$ & {row['y']} & {row['N_data']:.5f} & {row['N_MT']:.5f}"
                     f" & {row['V_over_sumMT']:.5f} & {row['N_h']:.5f} \\\\")
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_shape.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Appendix tables: all normalised values
    for i, name in enumerate(NAMES):
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        xs = sorted({r['x'] for r in p['rows']})
        lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{l' + 'r' * len(RATIOS) + '}', r'\toprule',
                 r'$x$ & ' + ' & '.join(f'${r:g}$' for r in RATIOS) + r' \\', r'\midrule']
        for x in xs:
            vals = [next(r['normalised'] for r in p['rows'] if r['x'] == x and r['ratio_target'] == rt) for rt in RATIOS]
            lines.append(sci(x) + ' & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(v, 6) for v in vals) + r' \\')
        lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'tab_full_{i}.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Plot data
    for i, name in enumerate(NAMES):
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        xs = sorted({r['x'] for r in p['rows']})
        last = sorted([r for r in all_rows(results, name) if r['x'] == xs[-1]], key=lambda r: r['ratio_actual'])
        txt = 'r sqrtr N\n' + ''.join(f"{r['ratio_actual']:.10g} {math.sqrt(r['ratio_actual']):.10g} {r['normalised']:.10g}\n" for r in last)
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_ratio_{i}.dat', txt))
        C, a, b = fitsum[name]['fit_coefficients']
        grid = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)
        txt = 'r sqrtr N\n' + ''.join(f'{r:.6g} {math.sqrt(r):.6g} {C + a * math.sqrt(r) + b * r:.10g}\n' for r in grid)
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_fit_{i}.dat', txt))
        txt = 'sqrtr N\n0 ' + f"{consts[name]['value']:.10g}\n"
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_cf_{i}.dat', txt))
        for rt, tag in [(.01, 'a'), (1., 'b')]:
            rr = sorted([r for r in p['rows'] if r['ratio_target'] == rt], key=lambda r: r['x'])
            txt = 'x N\n' + ''.join(f"{r['x']} {r['normalised']:.10g}\n" for r in rr)
            arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_x_{i}{tag}.dat', txt))
    for name in ['k^2+1', 'k^3+2']:
        i = NAMES.index(name)
        rr = sorted([s for s in shape if s['poly'] == name and s['x'] == SHAPE_XS[name][-1]], key=lambda s: s['ratio_actual'])
        txt = 'sqrtr Ndata NMT Nh\n' + ''.join(f"{math.sqrt(s['ratio_actual']):.8g} {s['N_data']:.10g} {s['N_MT']:.10g} {s['N_h']:.10g}\n" for s in rr)
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_shape_{i}.dat', txt))

    # Numbers quoted in the prose of Section 10, with checks of the qualitative
    # statements made there (the script stops if one of them fails).
    xl = max(r['x'] for r in results['polynomials']['k^2+1']['rows'])
    lastrow = {name: {r['ratio_target']: r for r in all_rows(results, name) if r['x'] == xl} for name in NAMES}
    stab = {name: max(abs(s_['relative_change']) for s_ in results['polynomials'][name]['stability']) for name in NAMES}
    ndiag = [lastrow[n][.005]['normalised'] for n in NAMES]
    none_ = [lastrow[n][1.]['normalised'] for n in NAMES]
    betas = [fitsum[n]['beta_fixed_x'] for n in NAMES]
    sens_q = [fitsum['k^2+1'][k] for k in ['C_extrapolated', 'previous_x_fit']] + \
             [fitsum['k^2+1']['alternative_models'][k] for k in ['sqrt', 'sqrt+linear+threehalves']] + \
             [fitsum['k^2+1']['upper_window_fits']['0.1'], fitsum['k^2+1']['cutoff_fits']['0.005']]
    cutoffs = {results['polynomials'][n]['constant_extrapolated']['ratio_cutoff'] for n in NAMES}
    all_elig = [e for n in NAMES for e in elig[n]]
    best = max(all_elig, key=lambda e: e['delta_max'])
    claims = {
        'stability below 1% at every ratio': max(stab.values()) < 0.01,
        'k^2+1 and 2k+1 change much less than k^3+2': max(stab['k^2+1'], stab['2k+1']) < stab['k^3+2'] / 10,
        'one common stable cutoff': len(cutoffs) == 1,
        'extrapolations within their envelopes': all(abs(fitsum[n]['difference_in_envelopes']) <= 1 for n in NAMES),
        'k^2+1 sensitivity range brackets C_f': min(sens_q) < consts['k^2+1']['value'] < max(sens_q),
        'rows with r <= 0.01 outside the range for every delta': all(e['delta_max'] < 0 for e in all_elig if e['ratio_target'] <= .01),
        'C_t and Vaughan c_2 agree to 1e-8 at N=1e7': abs(consts['t']['value'] - c2[PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]]) < 1e-8,
    }
    if not all(claims.values()):
        raise RuntimeError(f'a statement of Section 10 is not supported by the data: {claims}')
    pct = lambda v: f'{100 * v:+.2f}'

    # Macros for numbers quoted in the text
    macros = {
        'CfQuadCert': certified_digits(consts['k^2+1']['lower'], consts['k^2+1']['upper']),
        'CfCubicCert': certified_digits(consts['k^3+2']['lower'], consts['k^3+2']['upper']),
        'CfLinCert': certified_digits(consts['2k+1']['lower'], consts['2k+1']['upper']),
        'CfTCert': certified_digits(consts['t']['lower'], consts['t']['upper']),
        'FloatCheck': tex_sci(max(floatcheck.values())),
        'StabCubic': f"{100 * stab['k^3+2']:.2f}",
        'StabOther': f"{100 * max(stab['k^2+1'], stab['2k+1']):.2f}",
        'NDiagMin': f'{min(ndiag):.3f}', 'NDiagMax': f'{max(ndiag):.3f}',
        'NOneMin': f'{min(none_):.3f}', 'NOneMax': f'{max(none_):.3f}',
        'BetaMin': f'{min(betas):.3f}', 'BetaMax': f'{max(betas):.3f}',
        'StableCutoff': f'{cutoffs.pop():g}',
        'RelQuad': pct(fitsum['k^2+1']['relative_difference']),
        'RelCubic': pct(fitsum['k^3+2']['relative_difference']),
        'RelLin': pct(fitsum['2k+1']['relative_difference']),
        'SensQuadMin': f'{min(sens_q):.3f}', 'SensQuadMax': f'{max(sens_q):.3f}',
        'XLargeInvCubeSmall': f'{xl ** (-1 / 3) * .01 ** -1.5:.1f}',
        'XLargeInvCubeOne': tex_sci(xl ** (-1 / 3)),
        'XTwoNinths': f'{xl ** (-2 / 9):.4f}',
        'DeltaRowOneMax': tex_sci(max(e['delta_max'] for e in all_elig if e['ratio_target'] == 1.)),
        'DeltaRowMax': f"{best['delta_max']:.3f}",
        'DeltaRowMaxR': f"{best['ratio_target']:g}",
        'CfQuad': f"{consts['k^2+1']['value']:.8f}", 'CfCubic': f"{consts['k^3+2']['value']:.8f}",
        'CfLin': f"{consts['2k+1']['value']:.8f}", 'CfT': f"{consts['t']['value']:.8f}",
        'VaughanCtwo': f"{c2[PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]]:.8f}",
        'IConst': mp.nstr(I_CONST, 12),
        'ShapeMin': f"{min(s['V_over_sumMT'] for s in shape):.4f}",
        'ShapeMax': f"{max(s['V_over_sumMT'] for s in shape):.4f}",
        'ShapeRows': str(len(shape)),
        'ShapeDevLargest': tex_sci(max(abs(s['V_over_sumMT'] - 1) for s in shape if s['x'] == 256000000)),
        'SelfTest': tex_sci(selftest),
        'RerunMaxRelV': tex_sci(max(c['max_relative_difference_V'] for c in compare.values())),
        'RhoBound': str(1000),
    }
    tex = ''.join(f'\\newcommand{{\\{k}}}{{{v}}}\n' for k, v in macros.items())
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'macros.tex', tex))

    (GEN / 'snapshot_rerun_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1) + '\n')
    arts.append('generated/snapshot_rerun_results.json')

    repro = dict(
        description='All tables and plot data in the manuscript are generated by manuscript/reproduce.py; '
                    'see the per-artifact provenance below.',
        artifacts=arts,
        artifact_sources={
            'generated/tab_largest.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: results.json rows at the largest x, '
                                         'diagnostic ratio 0.005 rows, and stability (relative change between the two largest x).',
            'generated/tab_fits.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: fit_fixed_ratio, fit_fixed_x, constant_extrapolated; '
                                      'C_f from reproduce.py euler_constant (primes <= 1e7).',
            'generated/tab_sensitivity.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: constant_extrapolated alternative_models, '
                                             'upper_ratio_window_fits, cutoff_fits, previous_x_fit.',
            'generated/tab_constants.tex': 'reproduce.py euler_constant and vaughan_c2 (not part of the snapshot); '
                                           'partial products rounded to 9 decimals, interval endpoints rounded outwards.',
            'generated/tab_shape.tex': 'V from the snapshot re-run; sum f\'(k) MT(x;f(k)) and sum F(k) h(f(k)) '
                                       'from reproduce.py Arithmetic.MT / Arithmetic.h.',
            'generated/tab_full_*.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: normalised values of all primary rows.',
            'generated/fig_ratio_*.dat, fig_x_*.dat': 'snapshot compute.py re-run rows.',
            'generated/fig_fit_*.dat': 'snapshot primary fit N(r)=C+a sqrt(r)+b r (coefficients from the re-run).',
            'generated/fig_cf_*.dat': 'reproduce.py euler_constant.',
            'generated/fig_shape_*.dat': 'as tab_shape.tex, at the largest x.',
            'generated/macros.tex': 'numbers quoted in the text, from the computations above (C_f digits fixed by the '
                                    'intervals, stability, fit and sensitivity ranges, eligibility of rows for Theorem 1.1(iii), '
                                    'self-test and shape statistics); see text_claim_checks.',
            'generated/snapshot_rerun_results.json': 'results.json written by the re-run of the snapshot compute.py (all rows and fits).',
        },
        snapshot_rerun=dict(seconds=elapsed, total_seconds_of_reproduce_py=None, comparison_with_archived_results=compare,
                            note='compute.py and counts.cpp copied unchanged (SHA-256 checked); counts.cpp compiled locally by compute.py.'),
        constants={name: dict(partial={str(N): v for N, v in c['partial'].items()}, value=c['value'],
                              interval=[c['lower'], c['upper']], tail_log_bound=c['tail_log_bound'], K=c['K'])
                   for name, c in consts.items()},
        vaughan_c2={str(N): v for N, v in c2.items()},
        I=mp.nstr(I_CONST, 20), A0=mp.nstr(A0_mp(), 25),
        constants_float_check=dict(note='relative difference between the double-precision partial product '
                                        'for p <= 1e5 and a 40-digit mpmath recomputation; not a certified bound',
                                   values=floatcheck),
        constants_certified_digits={n: certified_digits(consts[n]['lower'], consts[n]['upper']) for n in consts},
        eligibility_at_largest_x=elig,
        text_claim_checks=claims,
        rho_formulas_checked_by_brute_force_for_primes_below=1000, rho_primes_checked=rho_checked,
        symbolic_checks=symb,
        identity_selftest_max_relative_discrepancy=selftest,
        fits=fitsum,
        exact_shape_rows=shape,
        parameters=dict(prime_cutoffs=PRIME_CUTOFFS, shape_xs=SHAPE_XS, ratios=RATIOS,
                        MT_head_terms_in_80_digit_arithmetic=Arithmetic.TSTAR),
        caveats='Fitted constants and their envelopes come from the snapshot code; the envelopes are heuristic '
                'sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals. C_f intervals bound only the omitted primes; '
                'floating-point rounding is not included (see constants_float_check for an uncertified check).',
    )
    return repro


def write_reproduction(repro, total):
    repro['snapshot_rerun']['total_seconds_of_reproduce_py'] = total
    (HERE / 'reproduction.json').write_text(json.dumps(repro, indent=2) + '\n')


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--work', type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_WORK,
                    help='scratch directory for the snapshot re-run (default: scratch/reproduce-work)')
    ap.add_argument('--reuse-work', action='store_true',
                    help='reuse results.json already present in the work directory instead of re-running the snapshot')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    results, elapsed = run_snapshot(args.work.resolve(), args.reuse_work)
    print(f'snapshot results ready ({elapsed if elapsed is not None else "reused"})', flush=True)
    compare = compare_with_archive(results)
    print('comparison with archived results:', json.dumps(compare), flush=True)
    P = primes_upto(PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1])
    rho_checked = {name: rho_bruteforce_check(name) for name in NAMES + ['t']}
    consts = {name: euler_constant(name, P) for name in NAMES + ['t']}
    c2 = vaughan_c2(P)
    symb = symbolic_local_identity()
    xmax = max(max(v) for v in SHAPE_XS.values())
    ar = Arithmetic(math.isqrt(xmax) + 2)
    selftest = identity_selftest(ar)
    print(f'identity self-test: max relative discrepancy {selftest:.2e}', flush=True)
    if selftest > 1e-8:
        raise RuntimeError('identity self-test failed')
    shape = shape_rows(results, ar)
    floatcheck = {}
    for name in NAMES + ['t']:
        exact = euler_float_check(name)
        floatcheck[name] = float(abs(consts[name]['partial'][10 ** 5] / exact - 1))
    print('float check of the Euler products:', floatcheck, flush=True)
    elig = {name: eligibility(results, name) for name in NAMES}
    repro = make_outputs(results, compare, consts, c2, shape, selftest, symb, rho_checked, elapsed, floatcheck, elig)
    write_reproduction(repro, time.monotonic() - t0)
    print(f'done in {time.monotonic() - t0:.1f}s; wrote {HERE / "reproduction.json"}', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

The sparse variance of squarefree numbers in arithmetic
   progressions to polynomial moduli: an elementary asymptotic
                              formula
                    Write-up of an archived machine-generated proof run
                                (provenance in Appendix B)


                                                        Abstract
         For a polynomial f ∈ Z[t] of degree d ≥ 1 with f (t) ≥ 2 and f ′ (t) ≥ 1 for t ≥ 1, consider
                                                        f (k)
                                       X                X                                     2
                        Vf (x, y) =           f ′ (k)           Q(x; f (k), l) − g(f (k), l) x ,
                                      1≤k≤y             l=1

     where Q(x; q, l) counts squarefree n ≤ x with n ≡ l (mod q) and g(q, l) is the corresponding
     density. We show by elementary means that Vf (x, y) = Cf x1/2 f (y)3/2 1 + O(x−η ) uniformly
                                                                                       

     for x7/9+δ ≤ f (y) ≤ x1−δ , with an explicit Euler product Cf > 0 and η = min(δ/12, 1/(6d)).
     We also give explicit error terms valid throughout f (y) ≤ x, and a version with an exact
     arithmetic main term. The proof rests on an exact identity for the variance with respect to a
     single modulus, a uniform count of pairs of P squarefree numbers with a given difference, an
     Euler–Maclaurin analysis of sawtooth sums s B(Z/s2 ), and an average of a multiplicative
     function over polynomial values. We compare the result with exact numerical computations
     of Vf for f = k 2 + 1, k 3 + 2 and 2k + 1 up to x = 2.56 · 108 .


Contents
1 Introduction                                                                                          2
  1.1 The problem . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .           2
  1.2 Background . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .          3
  1.3 The main result . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .         3
  1.4 Strategy . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .        4

                                J. BRÜDERN AND T. D. WOOLEY∗

        Abstract. An analogue of the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula is established
        for the variance of the number of primes in arithmetic progressions, in which the moduli
        are restricted to the values of a polynomial.




                                        1. Introduction
  The distribution of primes is a fundamental problem in the theory of numbers. Our
concern here is with the error terms that arise in the prime number theorem for arithmetic
progressions. Let 𝜙 denote Euler’s totient, and deﬁne the relevant quantity 𝐸(𝑥; 𝑘, 𝑙) for

154-   Sums of square-free numbers and similar problems involving k-free numbers were first investigated by
155:Evelyn and Linfoot in a series of papers (see Linfoot & Evelyn (1929) and Evelyn & Linfoot (1931), and
156-also Estermann (1931) and Mirsky (1947, 1948)). In cases in which there are s summands, with s ≥ 3,
157-they used the circle method to obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of representations in the
158-proposed manner. In the case s = 2, however, their circle method approach fails, and they remark that
159-“though the analytic method is still applicable in principle, there seems little hope of its furnishing a
160:practicable proof in this case”. Indeeed, for the binary problem Evelyn and Linfoot were forced to make
161-use of an elementary argument which yields the formula rk (n) = Sk (n)n + Oε,k (n2/(k+1)+ε ). Thus,
162-while Corollary 3 yields a weaker error term, it at least addresses the problem implicit in the above
163:remark of Evelyn and Linfoot. Moreover the flexibility of the circle method offers certain advantages
164-over the elementary methods. For example, one can obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of
165-representations of a given integer as the sum of a positive k-free number and a positive l-free number.
166-It is not clear in general how to approach such a problem via the elementary methods, the inherent
167-difficulty being one of obtaining suitable bounds for the number of integral solutions (x, y) of equations
168-of the shape axk + by l = n. Furthermore, our methods should yield sharper error terms than those of
169:Evelyn and Linfoot when the number of summands exceeds two.
170-   As a final application of Corollary 1 we provide a result concerning square-free numbers represented
171-as sums of three cubes. Denote by N (x) the number of integers, n, with 1 ≤ n ≤ x, such that n is
172-square-free and n is the sum of three cubes of positive integers.
173-Corollary 4. One has N (x)  x11/12 .
174-                                 11
175-   We remark that the exponent 12    could be replaced by one very slightly larger by making full use of
176-Theorem 1.2 of Wooley (1995). However, in the present circumstances expedience seems preferable to
177-precision. Again, Corollary 4 seems to be difficult to establish through elementary methods.
