\section{Provenance}\label{app:provenance}

The mathematics in \cref{sec:prelim,sec:densities,sec:identity,sec:pairs,sec:sawtooth,sec:single,sec:poly,sec:assembly} is an edited presentation of an archived run of a multi-agent proof pipeline in which language models proposed, proved and refereed the results. This appendix records where the material comes from. A proposition-by-proposition map, with every editorial change and correction, is in \texttt{manuscript/changes.md}.

\emph{Archive.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Source repository: \url{https://gitlab.com/mshepherd/squarefree-numbers}, archive label \texttt{zt-neutral}.
\item Archive commit: \texttt{ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba}.
\item Harness commit: \texttt{33aadc609359221ba5d81664438bce5f658f561c}.
\item Revision recorded for all run stages: \texttt{8dfc53d01e56c9949c42061fdbe907a98a12a5d7}.
\end{itemize}

\emph{Models and roles (as recorded).} The model identifiers are those recorded in the archive. The command-line tool versions are not model-weight versions, and model versions beyond these identifiers are unknown.
\begin{itemize}[before=\raggedright]
\item Planning and probing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}; probing also \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5}.
\item Numerics: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} produced candidate computations. The \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} snapshot was accepted.
\item Proofs: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} (prover).
\item Refereeing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}. Each proposition was reviewed independently by both.
\item Integration (assembly audit): \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}, independently.
\end{itemize}
Claude models ran under Claude Code 2.1.309 and Codex models under codex-cli 0.166.0.

\emph{Write-up stage.} This text was written by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} (Claude Code 2.1.311) from the archived run. It was refereed by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} (the write-up stage records Claude Code 2.1.311 and codex-cli 0.166.0) in two rounds. Each round was followed by a revision, and the present version answers the second round. Some of the corrections described below were raised by these write-up referees.

\emph{Workflow.} The problem statement restricts $f$ to $\Z[t]$. It asks for the asymptotic behaviour of $V_f(x,y)$ in as large a range of $f(y)\le x$ as can be justified, and it accepts a weaker range or error term provided it is correct. The weight $f'(k)$ and the class~\eqref{eq:f-hyp} of polynomials used here are those of the problem statement; neither was changed. The numerical candidates were computed before any plan existed, and one was accepted on computational grounds only, not because of its fitted constants. Eight proof plans were written, and the plan \texttt{simplest@claude-opus-5-5} was selected by the project owner. It splits the argument into nine propositions P1--P9. In this text, P1 is \cref{prop:densities}, P2 is \cref{prop:identity}, P3 is \cref{prop:pairs}, P4 is \cref{prop:trivial}, P5 is \cref{prop:sawtooth}, P6 is \cref{prop:MT}, P7 is \cref{prop:single}, P8 is \cref{prop:poly}, and P9 is \cref{thm:main} with its proof in \cref{sec:assembly}. All nine proofs passed both referees in the first round, with only cosmetic remarks. Both integrators found that the propositions compose to the stated theorem without loss and without interface mismatches. The project owner's recorded decision reads: ``Let's just assume the proof is correct and complete.'' A separate read-only operator audit found no substantive gap and left final mathematical acceptance to the project owner. The corrections made in this text are local and fall into three groups, listed individually in \texttt{changes.md}: (a) those recorded in the operator audit (the normalisation and convergence wording in P1(iii), the endpoint $k=1$ in P8, and unused numerical remarks in P6 and P8); (b) cosmetic points raised by the run's referees; and (c) points raised at the write-up stage. Group~(c) contains one change to an archived auxiliary statement. \Cref{lem:EM} narrows the infinite-interval case of the Euler--Maclaurin lemma in the archived P5 proof, which is false as stated there, by adding a convergence hypothesis. Every application in the archived argument satisfies that hypothesis, so no proposition and no step of the argument changes. This change is not covered by the recorded audit and is flagged in \texttt{changes.md} for the project owner's acknowledgement. The other items in group~(c) concern only the exposition of this text, for example an arithmetic slip in an earlier version of the write-up, and do not touch the archived arguments. Agreement between models is evidence, not certification; the arguments are reproduced here in full so that they can be checked directly.

\emph{Independent checks during the run.} Before acceptance, the operator compared both numerical candidates on overlapping rows and recomputed some rows by brute force. One integrator recomputed all $16$ rows for $k^2+1$ and $k^3+2$ at $x=250000$ by direct counting. The other computed $\sum f'(k)\MT(x;f(k))$ independently and compared it with the data. These checks are recorded in the archive. The computations in \cref{sec:numerics} were redone for this write-up as described there.

\emph{Literature.} The run used the papers supplied with the problem and literature up to 2010, with the single exception of Brüdern--Wooley~\cite{BruedernWooley2011}, which was supplied. The present text cites only works in the supplied corpus. See \texttt{README.md} for the limitations of the bibliography.

**actual** ratios. They reproduce the saved coefficients and intercept
  standard errors to within $10^{-12}$. The coefficients are
  $(0.13447470549221466,0.05829819823814369,-0.020881393324478102)$
  and
  $(0.13632125683949853,0.037554586806314995,-0.006861994814706394)$.
* The original numerical source code is not present. An independent
  direct squarefree sieve and residue-class enumeration reproduced all
  eight production rows for each polynomial at $x=250000$. For each
  modulus, the density was constructed from its local factors:
  $g=(6/\pi^2)q^{-1}\prod_{p\mid q}(1-p^{-2})^{-1}$, multiplied by
  $1-1/p$ on classes divisible by $p\parallel q$, and set to zero on
  classes divisible by $p^2\mid q$. Summing the squared errors with
  weights $2k$ or $3k^2$ matched the saved variances with maximum
  relative differences $6.67\times10^{-16}$ and $2.23\times10^{-16}$.
  All 16 weighted integer sums of $Q^2$ matched exactly. This is an
  independent check of representative raw counts and density terms;
  it is not a rerun of the largest production size.

At fixed positive $Y/x$, the P6 error need not decrease relative to the
main term, which explains why a fixed-ratio row is not an estimator of
$C_f$ by itself. The square-root extrapolation model is an empirical
choice in `results.json`; the passed propositions establish the weaker
power bound displayed in (17), not an exact expansion in $\sqrt{Y/x}$.
The extrapolated evidence is consistent with the constants above, within
its stated limitations, and does not constitute an additional proof.

Both bounds are absolute constants, independent of $q$ and $x$. So
$$|R|\le c(\epsilon)C_1C_2\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\epsilon}.$$
No use was made of $q\le x$ or $x\ge1$ in this step; the error bound holds for all $x>0$, $q\ge1$.

## Step 3: the constant equals $h(q)$
## Conclusion

For all real $x>0$ (in particular $x\ge1$) and all integers $q\ge1$ (in particular $1\le q\le x$),
$$\big|MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\big|\le C_1C_2\,c(\epsilon)\;x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\epsilon},$$
where $O_1(Y)$ denotes a quantity of modulus at most $Y$. By (0) with $z=\sqrt x\ge1$, the middle term has modulus at most $x\cdot 2/\sqrt x=2\sqrt x$. Therefore $|Q(x)-6x/\pi^2|\le 3\sqrt x$ for all $x\ge1$.

## (ii)

Fix $q\ge1$ (the hypothesis $q\le x$ will not be needed). Let $q_1=\prod_{p\,\|\,q}p$, the product of the primes dividing $q$ exactly once.
## Conclusion

Take $c_0=\max(3,3B)=3e^{2\zeta(3/2)}$. Then (i) holds for all real $x\ge1$ by the first part. Part (ii) holds for all real $x\ge1$ and all integers $q\ge1$, in particular for $1\le q\le x$. $\qquad\blacksquare$
7:Then $C_x(m)=\sum_{1\le n\le N}\mu^2(n)\mu^2(n+m)$. All implied constants below depend only on $\varepsilon$. Put $\tau^*=\max_{k\le x}\tau(k)\ll_\varepsilon x^{\varepsilon}$; this also bounds $\tau(m)$.
24:$$C_x(m)=\sum_{n\le N}S(n)S(n+m)+\mathcal E_1,\qquad |\mathcal E_1|\le\sum_{n\le N}|R(n)|+\tau^*\sum_{n\le N}|R(n+m)|.$$
28:Therefore $|\mathcal E_1|\le 2(1+\tau^*)x^{2/3}\ll x^{2/3+\varepsilon}$.
42:\le 2\cdot\frac{\pi^2}{6}\sum_{e^2\mid m}\frac1{e^2}\cdot\frac{2e}{z}\le\frac{4\pi^2}{3z}\sum_{e^2\mid m}\frac1e\le\frac{14\,\tau(m)}{z}.$$
44:$$N\sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\le z\\ (d_1,d_2)^2\mid m}}\frac{\mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)}{L}=N\Sigma+\mathcal E_3,\qquad|\mathcal E_3|\le \frac{14\,x\,\tau^*}{z}\ll x^{2/3+\varepsilon}.$$
61:$$|D_x(m)|\le 2(1+\tau^*)x^{2/3}+x^{2/3}+14\,\tau^*x^{2/3}\ll_\varepsilon x^{2/3+\varepsilon},$$
62:uniformly for real $x\ge2$ and integers $1\le m\le x$, since $\tau^*\ll_\varepsilon x^{\varepsilon}$. $\qquad\blacksquare$
## (iii) Squarefree $n$

Only squarefree $d$ contribute. For squarefree $d$, $g_d=\prod_{p\mid d}\gcd(p^2,q)$, the factors being powers of distinct primes and hence pairwise coprime. So $g_d\mid n$ iff $\gcd(p^2,q)\mid n$ for every $p\mid d$. Hence for squarefree $d$ the summand $q\cdot\mu(d)\frac{g_d}{d^2}\mathbf 1[g_d\mid n]$ equals $\prod_{p\mid d}h(p)$ with
$$h(p):=-\frac{\gcd(p^2,q)}{p^2}\mathbf 1[\gcd(p^2,q)\mid n].$$
As $\sum_p|h(p)|\le\sum_p p^{-2}<\infty$, the sum over squarefree $d$ of $\prod_{p\mid d}h(p)$ equals $\prod_p(1+h(p))$ (absolutely convergent Euler product). Now:

* $p\nmid q$: $\gcd(p^2,q)=1$, $h(p)=-p^{-2}$.

input.summary: I reviewed the manuscript independently against source/ (plan, the P1–P9 statements, proofs and both reviews, the integrator reports, interventions.md), the accepted numerical snapshot, provenance.json and the supplied papers. Theorem 1.1 is the archived main theorem and P9, with the same hypotheses, ranges, error terms, uniformity and constants: (i) error x^{1/3+ε}Y^{5/3}+x^{5/3+ε}+x^{1/2+ε}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}; (ii) error x^{5/3+ε}+x^{1/2}Y; (iii) the range x^{7/9+δ}≤f(y)≤x^{1-δ} with η=min(δ/12,1/(6d)). The weight f'(k) and the class of f are unchanged. I re-derived every proof line by line (Sections 2–9) and found no mathematical error. Every merged argument and dependency is used inside its contract. The corrections the audit authorised (P1(iii) normalisation and convergence, the P8 endpoint, the unused numerical notes) are carried out correctly. The other local corrections in changes.md are also correct and do not change any archived proposition statement. One of them narrows the b=∞ clause of the archived Euler–Maclaurin lemma, which is false as stated in the archive. It is properly flagged for Markus's acknowledgement. It is not a source gap: both archived applications satisfy the added hypothesis. All numerical claims hold up. Tables and plots come from a hash-checked re-run of the snapshot code, and the re-run output equals the archive. My own independent computations agree: brute-force V_f matches the archive to about 1e-16, and my separate MT code reproduces N_MT and V/Σ_MT. My C_f Euler products, Vaughan's c_2 and the refitted extrapolations also agree. Every citation checks against the supplied PDFs. Provenance matches provenance.json and claims no human authorship. The PDF is complete and readable, with no broken references. I raise only optional cosmetic remarks (listed in the check fields).
input.statement_checks: Theorem 1.1 against plan.md "Main theorem" and props/P9/statement.md. The hypotheses match: f∈Z[t], d≥1, f≥2 and f'≥1 for t≥1, read explicitly as real t, which is the reading the P9 referee confirmed. The ranges match: x≥2, y≥1, Y=f(y)≤x. The three error terms in (i) and (ii) match. In (iii), δ∈(0,1/9) is fixed and η=min(δ/12,1/(6d)). The positivity and finiteness of C_f match P8(0). σ_p equals the archived τ_p after renaming. I=-4ζ(-1/2)=ζ(3/2)/π, which I checked with the functional equation. The auxiliary statements match P1–P8: Prop 3.1 = P1(i)–(v); Prop 3.3 = P4, with c_0=3e^{2ζ(3/2)} taken from P4's conclusion; Prop 4.1 = P2 (an exact identity, x≥1, q∈N); Prop 5.1 = P3 (x≥2, 1≤m≤x); Prop 6.1 = P5(a)–(c), with c_1=60 from P5 line 37; Prop 6.2 = P6. Prop 6.2 is stated for all x>0 and q≥1; the P6 proof asserts exactly this at lines 50 and 71, and §4a records it. Prop 7.1 = P7 and Prop 8.1 = P8(0),(a)–(c). The changes.md §4a strengthenings each trace to the archived proofs, and none of them feeds a strengthening of the theorem. I re-derived the following myself: Lemma 2.2 (|θ|<1); the Prop 3.1(iii) local factors and (iv) through the (t,d',e') bijection and Lemma 2.5; Lemma 3.2 (3·2^ω√y); the P2 bookkeeping, in particular Σ_{j≤X}(X−j)=(X²−X+B(X))/2 including the case N=0 and the cancellation of x²S_2 and 6x/π²; P3 Steps 1–4, including the corrected 2π²/(3z)≤7/z and the final 3+9C(ε); P5(a), the integration by parts and the continuation at s=−1/2; P5(b), (b.1) and the bounds on R_1…R_5, which total 449/8Λ<57Λ plus Λ/4, under 60Λ; P5(c), β=μ*κ_q and (p−1)²(p+2)=p³−3p+2; P6, the factorisation t=t_0t_1t_2, the main coefficient and the three local factors a_p, b_p, c_p; P8, Lemma 8.2's identities (also checked with sympy), z_p≤x_p, (8.2), the w-bounds, the Rankin tail, the short sum, the Euler product σ_p/a_p, the truncation at e≤y and Lemma 8.5 for arbitrary intervals; and the §9 bookkeeping, where ε=min(δ/12,1/(9d)) gives the three ratios x^{−δ/12}, x^{−17δ/12}·…, x^{−5/(18d)}. Remark 1.3's identity σ_p|_{ρ≡1}=C_{1,p}(1−p^{−2})² holds; I confirmed it symbolically. Optional cosmetic remarks, none blocking: the abstract does not repeat that δ∈(0,1/9) is fixed and that the implied constant depends on f and δ. Lemma 8.5 implicitly needs G bounded on J; in its only use, F is continuous on [1,y].
input.dependency_checks: Every dependency is used inside its contract. P7 uses P2 (x≥1), P3 (x≥2, 1≤m=hq≤x, at most x/q terms), P4 (x≥1, 1≤q≤x) and P6. P9 uses P7 with q=f(k)∈[2,x], which follows from monotonicity for real t≥1, and P8(a)–(c), with y^{−1/2}≤γ_0^{1/(2d)}Y^{−1/(2d)}. P6 uses P5(c) with Z_1>0 and (t_0,q)=1, exactly as stated. P5(c) uses P5(b) at Z/n² for every n, which (b) allows because it holds for all Z>0. I checked each correction in changes.md §4 against the source. Items 1–2 (P1(iii)) are correct: the factor q is removed, |u(p)|≤1 for p|q, and the product is absolutely convergent. Item 3 (P3 constant) is correct. Item 4 (P8 endpoint, via Lemma 8.5 for arbitrary intervals) is correct and needs no value of F left of 1. Item 5 (absorbing log W with ε≤1/8) is correct. Item 9 (Λ/4) and item 20 (449/8) are correct. Item 19 (Lemma 2.6, b=∞) is a valid narrowing. The archived clause "F,F'→0, F''∈L¹" is false as stated: G=cos(log u)/u satisfies those conditions, but ∫_1^X G=sin(log X) diverges. Both archived uses, u^{−s} with Re s>1 and Φ=Z/u²−Z²/u⁴, have absolutely convergent integrals, so the archived P5 argument stands as applied. The manuscript discloses this change and flags it for Markus's acknowledgement rather than presenting it as accepted. It is not a source gap. The composition matches both integration reports (composes=true, no interface mismatches). Limitation: the earlier write-up feedback files that changes.md mentions (feedback/0.json, feedback/1.json) are not in this workspace, so I could not check the round-1 and round-2 responses against them.
input.numerics_checks: Computation path. reproduce.py checks the SHA-256 hashes of compute.py and counts.cpp against accepted.json; I re-hashed both and they match. It copies them, recompiles them and re-runs the snapshot, and reproduce.log shows a full run of all 11 sizes. generated/snapshot_rerun_results.json equals the archived results.json apart from the runtime fields; I compared them structurally. The tables are generated from the re-run output, not copied, and tab_full_* agrees exactly with the archived normalised values. All artifact hashes and the PDF hash match build-inputs.json; its accepted_snapshot field is sha256 of accepted.json's artifact manifest. I did not re-run reproduce.py, because it overwrites manuscript/generated. Instead I made these independent checks in referee-scratch/: (1) Brute-force V_f from definitions (sieve, residue counts, local-factor g), for k²+1 at x=2.5e5 (r=0.01, 0.1) and x=1e6 (r=0.01, 1), for k³+2 at 2.5e5 (r=0.05), and for 2k+1 at 2.5e5 (r=0.01). Each agrees with the archive to ≤3e−15 relative. (2) My own MT(x;q), using an exact tail with B(u)=u−u² and A_0 from the prime zeta function. It reproduces N_MT=0.1417124200, V/Σ_MT=1.0010036 and N_h=0.1396577 (k²+1, 1e6, r=0.01), and the rows 2k+1 at 2.5e5 (0.99381) and k²+1 at 1e6, r=1 (1.00003, N_h 0.13825). (3) C_f Euler products to 1e7: 0.13808262883, 0.13560752155, 0.14261331055, and formal t 0.12847866969, agreeing with Table 1 to about 1e−11. Vaughan's c_2 comes to 0.128478668188. The tail bound 8K(N^{−2}+1/(30N))/(1−K/N²) is correct, and the printed intervals and fixed digits are consistent with it. (4) Refitting C+a√r+br, the fixed-ratio slopes and the fixed-x β from results.json reproduces Table 3 exactly. The prose macros agree with the data: stability 0.91% and 0.04%, ranges 0.140–0.145 and 0.167–0.184, β 1.538–1.551, relative differences −2.61%, +0.53%, −0.65%, x^{−1/3}r^{−3/2} values of 1.6 and 1.6e−3, x^{−2/9}=0.0135, δ_row=0.103 at r=0.1 and ≤2.3e−4 at r=1, and shape range [0.9938, 1.0010]. I also checked the ρ formulas for the three polynomials by hand, including k³+2 at 2, 3, 4 and 9. The manuscript describes the envelopes correctly as heuristic and states that floating-point rounding is not certified.

structured_output.summary: I reviewed the manuscript independently against source/ (plan, the P1–P9 statements, proofs and both reviews, the integrator reports, interventions.md), the accepted numerical snapshot, provenance.json and the supplied papers. Theorem 1.1 is the archived main theorem and P9, with the same hypotheses, ranges, error terms, uniformity and constants: (i) error x^{1/3+ε}Y^{5/3}+x^{5/3+ε}+x^{1/2+ε}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}; (ii) error x^{5/3+ε}+x^{1/2}Y; (iii) the range x^{7/9+δ}≤f(y)≤x^{1-δ} with η=min(δ/12,1/(6d)). The weight f'(k) and the class of f are unchanged. I re-derived every proof line by line (Sections 2–9) and found no mathematical error. Every merged argument and dependency is used inside its contract. The corrections the audit authorised (P1(iii) normalisation and convergence, the P8 endpoint, the unused numerical notes) are carried out correctly. The other local corrections in changes.md are also correct and do not change any archived proposition statement. One of them narrows the b=∞ clause of the archived Euler–Maclaurin lemma, which is false as stated in the archive. It is properly flagged for Markus's acknowledgement. It is not a source gap: both archived applications satisfy the added hypothesis. All numerical claims hold up. Tables and plots come from a hash-checked re-run of the snapshot code, and the re-run output equals the archive. My own independent computations agree: brute-force V_f matches the archive to about 1e-16, and my separate MT code reproduces N_MT and V/Σ_MT. My C_f Euler products, Vaughan's c_2 and the refitted extrapolations also agree. Every citation checks against the supplied PDFs. Provenance matches provenance.json and claims no human authorship. The PDF is complete and readable, with no broken references. I raise only optional cosmetic remarks (listed in the check fields).
structured_output.statement_checks: Theorem 1.1 against plan.md "Main theorem" and props/P9/statement.md. The three error terms in (i) and (ii) match. In (iii), δ∈(0,1/9) is fixed and η=min(δ/12,1/(6d)). The positivity and finiteness of C_f match P8(0). σ_p equals the archived τ_p after renaming. I=-4ζ(-1/2)=ζ(3/2)/π, which I checked with the functional equation. The auxiliary statements match P1–P8: Prop 3.1 = P1(i)–(v); Prop 3.3 = P4, with c_0=3e^{2ζ(3/2)} taken from P4's conclusion; Prop 4.1 = P2 (an exact identity, x≥1, q∈N); Prop 5.1 = P3 (x≥2, 1≤m≤x); Prop 6.1 = P5(a)–(c), with c_1=60 from P5 line 37; Prop 6.2 = P6. Prop 6.2 is stated for all x>0 and q≥1; the P6 proof asserts exactly this at lines 50 and 71, and §4a records it. Prop 7.1 = P7 and Prop 8.1 = P8(0),(a)–(c). The changes.md §4a strengthenings each trace to the archived proofs, and none of them feeds a strengthening of the theorem.
